functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTupleError::OpaqueDataTupleError
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTupleError::OpaqueDataTupleError(const char* file, size_t line, const char* what)
functions.description: Constructs an OpaqueDataTupleError exception object describing an error related to OpaqueDataTuple operations. Intended to be thrown when tuple packing/unpacking or related actions fail.
requirements: Parameters file and what must point to valid, null-terminated C-strings for the duration of exception construction.
line should indicate the source line where the error occurred; no specific range constraints are documented.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::OpaqueDataTuple
functions.description: Default constructor that creates an empty OpaqueDataTuple with the specified length field type (1-byte or 2-bytes; LENGTH_EMPTY also exists). Use to build a tuple programmatically before packing.
requirements: length_field_type must be a valid enumerator (LENGTH_1_BYTE or LENGTH_2_BYTES are meaningful for on-wire use).
Tuple is initially empty.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::append
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::append(const char* data, const size_t len)
functions.description: Appends len bytes from a raw char buffer to the tuple’s data.
requirements: data must point to a buffer containing at least len bytes; behavior is undefined if len exceeds the actual buffer size.
len may be zero to append nothing (not explicitly restricted).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::assign
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::assign(const char* data, const size_t len)
functions.description: Replaces the tuple’s existing data with len bytes from a raw char buffer.
requirements: data must point to a buffer containing at least len bytes; behavior is undefined if len exceeds the actual buffer size.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::clear
functions.description: Removes the contents of the tuple, making its data empty.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::equals
functions.description: Returns true if the tuple’s data, interpreted in textual form, matches the provided string. Serves as a convenience comparator for string content.
requirements: Exact comparison semantics depend on getText(); specifics of textual conversion are not detailed in this header.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::getLengthFieldType
functions.description: Returns the configured length field type (1-byte or 2-bytes length field) for this tuple.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::getLength
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes currently stored in the tuple’s data.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::getTotalLength
functions.description: Returns the total on-wire size of the tuple: size of the length field plus the data length.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::getData
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the internal buffer holding the tuple data. Useful for direct access without copying.
requirements: The returned reference is only valid while the OpaqueDataTuple object exists; do not use it after the object is destroyed.
Callers must not modify the referenced buffer (const).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::getText
functions.description: Returns the tuple data in textual form. Intended for human-readable representation or string comparisons.
requirements: Exact encoding/format of the textual conversion is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::pack
functions.description: Serializes the tuple into wire format and appends it to buf: first the length field (1 or 2 bytes), then the data. Throws OpaqueDataTupleError if the tuple is malformed.
requirements: buf must be a valid OutputBuffer ready to accept appended bytes.
Tuple must not be empty (data length > 0) to be considered well-formed for packing.
If length_field_type is LENGTH_1_BYTE, data length must be <= 255; if LENGTH_2_BYTES, data length must be <= 65535.
On malformed tuples, the function throws OpaqueDataTupleError; callers should be prepared to catch exceptions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::unpack
functions.description: Parses wire-format data from [begin, end) into the tuple. Expects a length field of the configured size followed by at least that many data bytes. Allows zero-length data.
requirements: [begin, end) must contain at least the length field as defined by getDataFieldSize().
After consuming the length field, the remaining bytes must be >= the length value read; otherwise an exception is thrown.
Iterators must be valid and refer to the same underlying contiguous buffer range for the duration of the operation.
May throw on malformed input; callers should be prepared to catch exceptions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::operator=
functions.description: Assigns the provided string to the tuple’s data, replacing any existing content.
requirements: Equivalent to assign(other). No additional constraints beyond assign().

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::operator==
functions.description: Compares the tuple’s data (in textual form) to the provided string for equality.
requirements: Comparison semantics rely on getText(); exact conversion details are not specified in this header.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::operator!=
functions.description: Compares the tuple’s data (in textual form) to the provided string for inequality.
requirements: Comparison semantics rely on getText(); exact conversion details are not specified in this header.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple::getDataFieldSize
functions.description: Returns the size, in bytes, of the length field for this tuple, based on the configured LengthFieldType.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::operator<<
functions.signature: std::ostream& isc::dhcp::operator<<(std::ostream& os, const isc::dhcp::OpaqueDataTuple& tuple)
functions.description: Inserts the tuple’s textual representation into the output stream and returns the stream.
requirements: os must be a valid output stream.
tuple is formatted via its textual representation (as per getText()).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::operator>>
functions.description: Extracts data from the input stream and inserts it into the tuple, replacing any existing data. Specific parsing rules are not detailed in this header.
requirements: is must be a valid input stream.
Exact input format and error handling behavior are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::factory
functions.signature: static isc::dhcp::OptionPtr isc::dhcp::Option::factory(isc::dhcp::Option::Universe u, uint16_t type, const isc::dhcp::OptionBuffer& buf)
functions.description: Creates an Option instance of the specified universe and type using a registered factory for that type, initialized from the provided option buffer. Use when you already have raw option bytes to initialize the object. Throws if no factory is registered for the given type.
requirements: u must be either isc::dhcp::Option::V4 or isc::dhcp::Option::V6.
type must be valid for the universe (0-255 for V4; 0-65535 for V6).
buf points to the option payload (not including the on-wire header) and should contain the option data expected by the specific option type.
A factory for (u,type) must have been registered via LibDHCP::OptionFactoryRegister; otherwise an isc::InvalidOperation is thrown.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::create
functions.description: Allocates and returns a shared pointer to an Option instance owned by the Kea process, suitable for creation within hooks libraries that may be unloaded. Use for constructing options without initial data.
requirements: u must be either isc::dhcp::Option::V4 or isc::dhcp::Option::V6.
type must be valid for the universe (0-255 for V4; 0-65535 for V6).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::create
functions.signature: static isc::dhcp::OptionPtr isc::dhcp::Option::create(isc::dhcp::Option::Universe u, uint16_t type, const isc::dhcp::OptionBuffer& data)
functions.description: Allocates and returns a shared pointer to an Option instance owned by the Kea process, initialized with the provided data buffer. Intended for use in hooks libraries to ensure object ownership remains with Kea after library unload.
requirements: u must be either isc::dhcp::Option::V4 or isc::dhcp::Option::V6.
type must be valid for the universe (0-255 for V4; 0-65535 for V6).
data should contain the option payload appropriate for the option type (not including on-wire header).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::clone
functions.description: Returns a deep copy of this option, including all suboptions. Derived classes should override to return a copy of their concrete type (often by calling cloneInternal<T>).
requirements: May be called on a valid Option instance; returns a new OptionPtr which the caller must manage via shared_ptr semantics.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getUniverse
functions.description: Returns the option universe (V4 or V6).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::pack
functions.signature: virtual void isc::dhcp::Option::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes the option to wire format and appends it to the provided output buffer. For DHCPv4, when check is true, the function enforces the maximum option length (255 bytes for payload); for DHCPv6, code/length are written as 2-byte fields. Derived classes may override to include type-specific packing and suboptions.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable isc::util::OutputBuffer.
The option must have a valid universe (V4 or V6); otherwise a BadValue may be thrown.
If universe is V4 and check is true, the packed option length must not exceed 255 bytes; set check=false to bypass that limit when necessary.
Any suboptions contained must themselves be packable; exceptions from suboption packing may propagate.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::unpack
functions.description: Parses the provided buffer range as this option's payload and populates the option's internal data and suboptions as appropriate. Intended for received options.
requirements: begin and end must delimit a valid contiguous buffer range representing only the option payload (excludes on-wire header).
The range [begin,end) length must meet the minimum size required by the specific accessor used later (e.g., getUint16 requires at least 2 bytes, etc.).

Exceptions may be thrown on malformed input; callers should be prepared to handle parsing errors including OptionParseError, SkipRemainingOptionsError, or SkipThisOptionError from higher-level unpacking contexts.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable textual representation of the option, optionally indented. Useful for logging and diagnostics.
requirements: indent should be a non-negative number of spaces to prepend (negative values are unspecified).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::toString
functions.description: Returns a terse string representation of the option value, suitable for client classification and concise displays.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::toBinary
functions.signature: virtual std::vector<uint8_t> isc::dhcp::Option::toBinary(const bool include_header = false) const
functions.description: Returns a vector containing the binary representation of the option. By default only the payload is returned; when include_header is true, the on-wire header fields are included.
requirements: If include_header is true, the caller should expect the vector to begin with the universe-appropriate option code and length fields.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::toHexString
functions.signature: virtual std::string isc::dhcp::Option::toHexString(const bool include_header = false) const
functions.description: Returns a hexadecimal string representation of the option. By default only the payload is included; when include_header is true, the on-wire header is also included.
requirements: If include_header is true, the hexadecimal string will include the universe-appropriate header fields first.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getType
functions.description: Returns the numeric option code (0-255 for DHCPv4; 0-65535 for DHCPv6).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::len
functions.description: Returns the total on-wire length of the option (header length plus payload length) for the set universe.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getHeaderLen
functions.description: Returns the on-wire header length for this option: 2 bytes for DHCPv4 and 4 bytes for DHCPv6.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::valid
functions.description: Indicates whether the option appears valid (e.g., not truncated). Exact validation criteria may depend on the concrete option type.
requirements: Interpretation of validity is option-type-specific; callers should not assume deep semantic validation beyond basic structural checks.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getData
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the option payload buffer. If the option has no data, an empty vector reference is returned.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the Option object exists and is not modified in a way that would reallocate the buffer.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::addOption
functions.description: Adds a suboption to this option. Used by option types that encapsulate other options (e.g., certain DHCPv6 options).
requirements: opt should be a non-null shared pointer to a valid Option instance.
Suboptions are stored in this option’s internal collection and may affect packing and text rendering.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getOption
functions.description: Returns the first suboption with the specified type, or null if none exists.
requirements: type is the suboption code to search for. If multiple suboptions of the same type exist, only the first is returned.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getOptions
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the multimap of encapsulated suboptions.
requirements: The returned reference is valid only as long as the parent Option object exists.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getMutableOptions
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the multimap of encapsulated suboptions. Changes to this container directly affect the option content.
requirements: The returned reference is valid only as long as the parent Option object exists.
Callers are responsible for maintaining any invariants expected by the option type when mutating the collection.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getOptionsCopy
functions.description: Performs a deep copy of all suboptions into the provided container by cloning each suboption.
requirements: options_copy must be a valid container that will be cleared or appended to according to caller’s usage; it is populated with deep-copied suboptions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::delOption
functions.description: Deletes the first suboption of the specified type if present.
requirements: type is the suboption code to remove.
Returns true if a suboption was removed; false otherwise.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getUint8
functions.description: Returns the first byte of the option payload as uint8_t.
requirements: The option payload length must be at least 1 byte; otherwise isc::OutOfRange is thrown.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getUint16
functions.description: Returns the first two bytes of the option payload as a uint16_t value.
requirements: The option payload length must be at least 2 bytes; otherwise isc::OutOfRange is thrown.
Interpretation of endianness follows the option’s wire format (network byte order).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getUint32
functions.description: Returns the first four bytes of the option payload as a uint32_t value.
requirements: The option payload length must be at least 4 bytes; otherwise isc::OutOfRange is thrown.
Interpretation of endianness follows the option’s wire format (network byte order).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::setUint8
functions.description: Sets the option payload to a single uint8_t, resizing the payload to exactly 1 byte.
requirements: No special requirements; the payload is resized to 1 byte and overwritten.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::setUint16
functions.description: Sets the option payload to a single uint16_t value, resizing the payload to exactly 2 bytes.
requirements: No special requirements; the payload is resized to 2 bytes and overwritten.
Value is stored according to the option’s wire format (network byte order).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::setUint32
functions.description: Sets the option payload to a single uint32_t value, resizing the payload to exactly 4 bytes.
requirements: No special requirements; the payload is resized to 4 bytes and overwritten.
Value is stored according to the option’s wire format (network byte order).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::setEncapsulatedSpace
functions.description: Sets the name of the option space encapsulated by this option. Used by options that carry nested options.
requirements: encapsulated_space should be a valid option space name understood by the application’s configuration.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::getEncapsulatedSpace
functions.description: Returns the name of the option space encapsulated by this option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::~Option
functions.description: Virtual destructor to ensure proper cleanup via base-class pointers.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::equals
functions.description: Compares this option with another option (via shared pointer) for equality by delegating to the virtual equals overload. Not intended to be overridden.
requirements: other may be null; behavior when null is not specified in the header (callers should handle potential false or safeguards).
Equality semantics include type and content; for derived types, a proper override of virtual equals(const Option&) should exist for meaningful comparisons.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option::equals
functions.signature: virtual bool isc::dhcp::Option::equals(const isc::dhcp::Option& other) const
functions.description: Virtual comparison for equality with another option instance. Default semantics compare option type and content; derived classes should override when richer semantics are required.
requirements: other must reference a valid Option instance.
When using derived types, ensure an appropriate override exists to avoid comparing base and derived inconsistently.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::Option4AddrLst
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv4 option that holds a list of IPv4 addresses, initially empty. Addresses can later be added via addAddress, setAddress, or setAddresses.
requirements: type must be a valid DHCPv4 option code in the range 0–255.
The constructed object holds no addresses until explicitly set or added.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this option object as an OptionPtr. Useful for duplicating options when building or relaying packets.
requirements: Caller must manage the returned smart pointer (OptionPtr).
Cloned option will contain a copy of the address list at the time of cloning.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::pack
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes the option into DHCP wire format and appends it to the provided OutputBuffer. If check is true, enforces DHCPv4 option-size limits; if false, allows larger-than-255-byte payloads for v4.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable isc::util::OutputBuffer.
If check is true, the serialized DHCPv4 option (including header rules enforced by implementation) must not exceed the protocol’s 255-byte option length limit; otherwise the method may throw.
Method may throw if storing/serialization fails.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string representation of the option, optionally preceded by indent spaces. Useful for logging/debugging.
requirements: indent is the number of leading spaces; non-negative values are expected (negative behavior is unspecified).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::len
functions.description: Returns the total length of the option in bytes, including the DHCPv4 option header and the data payload (addresses).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::getAddresses
functions.description: Returns a copy of the internal list of IPv4 addresses. Returning a copy ensures the list remains valid even if the option object is destroyed.
requirements: The returned container is a copy; modifying it does not affect the option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::setAddresses
functions.description: Replaces the current address list with the provided list of IPv4 addresses.
requirements: Each element of addrs must be an IPv4 address; otherwise a BadValue exception will be thrown.
Existing addresses in the option are cleared before setting the new list.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::setAddress
functions.description: Clears the current list and sets it to a single IPv4 address.
requirements: addr must be an IPv4 address; otherwise a BadValue exception will be thrown.
Existing addresses in the option are cleared prior to setting the new single address.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4AddrLst::addAddress
functions.description: Appends a single IPv4 address to the existing list of addresses in the option.
requirements: addr must be an IPv4 address; otherwise a BadValue exception will be thrown.

line should indicate the source line where the error occurred.
what must be a null-terminated C string describing the error.

line should indicate the source line where the error occurred.
what must be a null-terminated C string describing the error.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::Rcode::Rcode
functions.description: Constructs an Rcode wrapper for the RCODE1/RCODE2 value used in Option 81. Typically servers use 255 and clients use 0, but this type can carry any 8-bit value, including invalid ones received on the wire.
requirements: rcode is an 8-bit value; typical valid values are 0 (client) or 255 (server) per RFC 4702.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::Rcode::getCode
functions.description: Returns the encapsulated RCODE value suitable for on-wire encoding of the DHCPv4 Client FQDN option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::Option4ClientFqdn
functions.signature: explicit isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::Option4ClientFqdn(const uint8_t flags, const Rcode& rcode, const std::string& domain_name, const DomainNameType domain_name_type = FULL)
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv4 Client FQDN (option 81) with specified flags, RCODE1/RCODE2 value (same for both), and a domain name (partial or full). Intended for composing outgoing options.
requirements: flags must only use defined bits FLAG_S, FLAG_O, FLAG_E, FLAG_N; MBZ bits must be zero (i.e., (flags & ~FLAG_MASK) == 0) or InvalidOption4FqdnFlags may be thrown.
rcode sets both RCODE1 and RCODE2 to the same value; typical usage is RCODE_CLIENT() for clients and RCODE_SERVER() for servers.
domain_name must be a valid domain per the class’s validation rules; InvalidOption4FqdnDomainName is thrown on invalid input.
domain_name_type must correctly indicate whether domain_name is partial (no trailing dot) or full (trailing dot).
Domain names are case-insensitive and will be lowercased internally.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this Option4ClientFqdn as an OptionPtr. Use when duplicating options into other messages/contexts.
requirements: Caller must manage the returned smart pointer (OptionPtr).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::~Option4ClientFqdn
functions.description: Destructor for Option4ClientFqdn. Releases internal resources (pimpl).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::operator=
functions.description: Assignment operator copying state from another Option4ClientFqdn instance.
requirements: source must be a valid, initialized Option4ClientFqdn.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::getFlag
functions.description: Returns whether a specific flag bit (S, O, E, or N) is set in the flags field.
requirements: flag must be one of FLAG_S, FLAG_O, FLAG_E, FLAG_N; otherwise an invalid-flag exception is thrown (documentation refers to InvalidOption4ClientFlags; in this header the defined type is InvalidOption4FqdnFlags).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::setFlag
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::setFlag(const uint8_t flag, const bool set)
functions.description: Sets or clears a specific flag bit (S, O, E, or N) in the flags field.
requirements: flag must be one of FLAG_S, FLAG_O, FLAG_E, FLAG_N; otherwise an invalid-flag exception is thrown (documentation refers to InvalidOption4ClientFlags; in this header the defined type is InvalidOption4FqdnFlags).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::resetFlags
functions.description: Clears all flags (sets the flag field to 0).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::getRcode
functions.description: Returns the values of RCODE1 and RCODE2 as a pair of Rcode objects (first=RCODE1, second=RCODE2).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::setRcode
functions.description: Sets both RCODE1 and RCODE2 to the provided value.
requirements: rcode will be applied to both RCODE fields; typical values are RCODE_CLIENT() for clients and RCODE_SERVER() for servers.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::getDomainName
functions.description: Returns the domain name in text form. Full names include a trailing dot; partial names do not. Returned names are lower-cased.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::packDomainName
functions.description: Appends the domain name to the provided buffer in on-wire format (canonical wire format without compression if E=1, or ASCII if E=0 per RFC 4702).
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable OutputBuffer into which data can be appended.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::setDomainName
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::setDomainName(const std::string& domain_name, const DomainNameType domain_name_type)
functions.description: Sets the domain name value and whether it is partial or fully-qualified. Validates the name and stores a normalized (lowercase) form.
requirements: domain_name must pass validation or InvalidOption4FqdnDomainName will be thrown.
domain_name_type must correctly describe whether the name is partial or full.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4ClientFqdn::resetDomainName
functions.description: Sets the domain name to empty and marks it as partial. Exception-safe.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::packAdn
functions.description: Appends the Authentication Domain Name (as on-wire DNS name) to the provided output buffer.
requirements: ADN must be set and non-empty; otherwise InvalidOptionDnrDomainName is thrown.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::packAddresses
functions.description: Appends the encoded IP address list to the output buffer according to the option universe (IPv4 for DHCPv4, IPv6 for DHCPv6).
requirements: buf must be a valid OutputBuffer.
Addresses must be populated prior to packing unless ADN-only mode is enabled (inferred).
For DHCPv4 universe, only IPv4 addresses should be present; for DHCPv6 universe, IPv6 addresses should be present (inferred from documentation).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::packSvcParams
functions.description: Appends the encoded Service Parameters (SvcParams) to the output buffer using RFC9460 Section 2.2 encoding.
requirements: buf must be a valid OutputBuffer.
Forbidden SvcParams (ipv4hint, ipv6hint) must not be present (per FORBIDDEN_SVC_PARAMS; enforcement may occur during parsing earlier).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::unpackDnrInstanceDataLength
functions.description: Reads the DNR Instance Data Length from the input buffer and stores it. Used when parsing DHCPv4 DNR instances.
requirements: begin and end must delimit a buffer region containing at least the DNR Instance Data Length field; otherwise OutOfRange is thrown.
begin is advanced past the consumed field on success.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::unpackServicePriority
functions.description: Reads the Service Priority field from the input buffer and stores it.
requirements: begin must have at least 2 octets available for the Service Priority field; otherwise parsing by caller should ensure bounds (length checking responsibility implied by surrounding code).
begin is advanced past the consumed field on success.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::unpackAdn
functions.description: Parses the Authentication Domain Name (opaque on-wire DNS name) from the input buffer and stores it in the instance.
requirements: begin and end must delimit enough data for the ADN length and name per RFC8415 Section 10; otherwise BadValue or InvalidOptionDnrDomainName may be thrown.
begin is advanced past the consumed ADN data on success.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::unpackAddresses
functions.description: Parses the IP address list from the input buffer into the instance’s address container.
requirements: begin and end must delimit the Addr Length and address bytes; otherwise OutOfRange or BadValue may be thrown.
Addr Length must be non-zero and divisible by 4 for IPv4; similar well-formedness rules apply for IPv6 per implementation (documentation states divisibility by 4 and non-zero as examples).
begin is advanced past the consumed address bytes on success.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::unpackSvcParams
functions.description: Parses Service Parameters from the input buffer into the instance’s svc_params buffer/map, validating syntax per RFC9460 Section 2.2.
requirements: begin and end must delimit the SvcParams region; otherwise OutOfRange is thrown.
SvcParams syntax must be valid; otherwise InvalidOptionDnrSvcParams is thrown.
Forbidden parameters (ipv4hint, ipv6hint) are not allowed (per documentation).
begin is advanced past the consumed bytes on success.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::addIpAddress
functions.description: Adds an IP address to this instance’s address list.
requirements: ip_address must be a valid IOAddress instance.
For DHCPv4 universe, the address should be IPv4; for DHCPv6 universe, the address should be IPv6 (inferred from documentation describing address types per universe).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::DnrInstance::parseDnrInstanceConfigData
functions.description: Parses a single DNR instance specified in a convenient text notation into this object. Supports ADN-only mode. Handles escaping of commas and pipes via double backslash.
requirements: config_txt must follow the documented formats, e.g., "100, dot1.example.org., 2001:db8::1 2001:db8::2, alpn=dot\\,doq\\,h2\\,h3 port=8530 dohpath=/q{?dns}" for v6 or IPv4 equivalents; multiple instances for v4 must be parsed by calling this per-instance.
Improper format results in BadValue; invalid ADN results in InvalidOptionDnrDomainName; invalid SvcParams results in InvalidOptionDnrSvcParams.
When specifying SvcParams, forbidden keys (ipv4hint, ipv6hint) must not be included.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4Dnr::Option4Dnr
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::Option4Dnr::Option4Dnr(isc::dhcp::OptionBufferConstIter begin, isc::dhcp::OptionBufferConstIter end, bool convenient_notation = false)
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv4 Encrypted DNS (Option 162) from an input buffer. If convenient_notation is true, the buffer contains a text configuration string to be parsed; otherwise, it contains the binary on-wire format.
requirements: begin and end must delimit the full option data region.

If convenient_notation is true, the buffer content must be a valid UTF-8/text string matching parseConfigData’s expected format; otherwise BadValue/InvalidOptionDnrDomainName/InvalidOptionDnrSvcParams can propagate.
If convenient_notation is false, the binary must be well-formed; otherwise OutOfRange/BadValue/InvalidOptionDnrDomainName can be thrown via DnrInstance unpacking.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6AddrLst::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this Option6AddrLst as a polymorphic OptionPtr. Use when you need a duplicate option instance without sharing state.
requirements: The returned OptionPtr must be checked for null only if the caller’s environment allows exceptions to be disabled; otherwise clone is expected to succeed or throw (exact error behavior not specified)
Caller assumes ownership of the returned smart pointer and manages its lifetime via OptionPtr semantics

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6AddrLst::pack
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Option6AddrLst::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes the option into its on-wire format and appends it to the provided OutputBuffer. Intended for building outbound DHCP messages. The check flag controls size checks for v4 options; for this DHCPv6 option, typical usage leaves it as true.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable isc::util::OutputBuffer
This instance should be in a valid state (e.g., contains zero or more IPv6 addresses) before packing
If integrating with DHCPv4 contexts, setting check=false allows options larger than 255 bytes; for DHCPv6 this limit typically does not apply (note from interface)

The range length should be a multiple of 16 bytes (one or more IPv6 addresses) — inferred from the option’s purpose
Caller should ensure the provided bytes are the entire option data field (excluding the option header)
Caller should handle parse errors (e.g., invalid length) via the library’s error mechanism (exceptions or status), exact details not specified

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6AddrLst::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable textual representation of the option, optionally indented. Useful for logging and diagnostics.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6AddrLst::setAddresses

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::Option6Auth
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::Option6Auth(const uint8_t proto, const uint8_t algo, const uint8_t method, const uint64_t rdm, const std::vector<uint8_t>& info)
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv6 Authentication (option 11) object with the given protocol, hash algorithm, replay detection method, replay detection value, and authentication information. Intended for preparing/transmitting an Authentication option as defined in RFC 8415 §21.11.
requirements: proto, algo, and method are 8-bit values; rdm is a 64-bit value; info is arbitrary-length authentication data.
Caller should supply values consistent with the intended authentication scheme; no validation is enforced by this declaration.
Object is for DHCPv6 Authentication option usage.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::clone
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of this Option6Auth and returns it as an OptionPtr. Use when duplicating options without sharing mutable state.
requirements: The source object must be in a valid state (fields set via constructor/unpack/setters).
Caller must manage the returned smart pointer according to project conventions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::pack
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes the Authentication option to wire format and appends it to the provided OutputBuffer. Returns via side effect by advancing the buffer write position. The check flag (from Option interface) controls size checks (not typically relevant for DHCPv6).
requirements: buf must be a valid OutputBuffer ready for writing.
All required fields (protocol, algorithm, rdm method/value, and auth info) should be set before calling.
If using in DHCPv4 contexts, pass check=false to allow options > 255 bytes; for DHCPv6 this is generally not needed (as per comment).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::packHashInput
functions.description: Serializes the option into buf specifically for cryptographic hashing: the authentication info field is written as 128 bits (16 bytes) of zeroes to produce the canonical hash input.
requirements: buf must be a valid OutputBuffer ready for writing.
Intended for computing/validating authentication digests; do not use as the final option on the wire unless you intend the auth info to be zeroed.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::unpack
functions.description: Parses the option data from [begin, end) and populates this Option6Auth. Returns by advancing the provided iterators’ consumption implicitly (caller computes offset via distance used).
requirements: begin and end must form a valid range within a received option payload; begin <= end.
The range length must be at least OPTION6_AUTH_MIN_LEN (11 bytes) to hold protocol (1), algorithm (1), method (1), and 64-bit replay detection value.
Buffer must contain exactly the option data (not including outer option code/length if those are handled elsewhere in Option).
Iterators must remain valid during parsing.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the Authentication option, optionally prefixed with indent spaces.
requirements: indent should be non-negative; negative values may produce implementation-defined formatting.
Object should be in a valid state (constructed or unpacked) to produce meaningful output.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::setHashAlgo

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::setReplyDetectionMethod
functions.description: Sets the replay detection method type for the Authentication option.

functions.description: Sets the 64-bit replay detection value (RDM) carried in the Authentication option.
requirements: value is a 64-bit integer; no further constraints are enforced here.

functions.description: Sets the authentication information (message authentication code or related data) for the option.
requirements: auth_info may be any length per this declaration. For hashing via packHashInput the field is zeroed to 16 bytes in the hash input; callers preparing final on-wire auth data should supply appropriately sized data for their algorithm.

functions.description: Returns the protocol type value.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::getHashAlgo

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::getReplyDetectionMethod
functions.description: Returns the replay detection method type value.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Auth::getReplyDetectionValue

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6ClientFqdn::Option6ClientFqdn
functions.signature: explicit isc::dhcp::Option6ClientFqdn::Option6ClientFqdn(const uint8_t flags, const std::string& domain_name, const DomainNameType domain_name_type = FULL)
functions.description: Creates a DHCPv6 Client FQDN (option 39) instance for outgoing messages with specified flags and a domain name (partial or full). Domain names are normalized to lower case; empty domain names are accepted to signal server-generated FQDNs.
requirements: flags must only use the defined bits FLAG_S (0x01), FLAG_O (0x02), FLAG_N (0x04); MBZ bits must be zero (i.e., flags & ~FLAG_MASK must be 0).
domain_name may be empty; if not empty it must be a syntactically valid domain name per implementation rules; invalid names cause an exception.
domain_name_type must be either PARTIAL or FULL; FULL implies a trailing dot in text form, PARTIAL implies none.

functions.signature: virtual void isc::dhcp::Option6ClientFqdn::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes the entire option (including header and flags/domain) into the provided buffer in wire format. If check is false, allows options larger than 255 for v4 (not typically relevant for v6).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6ClientFqdn::unpack
functions.description: Parses the option from a buffer range [first, last) in wire format, populating flags and domain name. Throws on invalid length or malformed data.
requirements: first and last must form a valid range; first must be <= last and iterators must remain valid during parsing.
The range must contain at least the full option (including header). Insufficient data causes an exception.
Data must conform to DHCPv6 Client FQDN option structure (flags byte and encoded domain name).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6ClientFqdn::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string with the option's flags and domain name. Indents the output by the specified number of spaces.
requirements: indent should be non-negative (by convention); negative values may produce implementation-defined formatting.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6ClientFqdn::len
functions.description: Returns the total length of the option on the wire (payload plus DHCPv6 option header).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::Option6Dnr
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::Option6Dnr(OptionBufferConstIter begin, OptionBufferConstIter end, bool convenient_notation = false)
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv6 Encrypted DNS (option 144) object from on-wire data or from a convenient-notation string buffer. It initializes the option by parsing the provided byte range; parsing behavior may differ when convenient_notation is true. Throws if the buffer is truncated or if Authentication Domain Name (ADN) parsing fails.
requirements: begin and end must delimit a valid contiguous buffer containing the complete option payload (not truncated).
If convenient_notation is true, the buffer must contain a valid convenient-notation string acceptable to the parser.
ADN data in the buffer must be valid; otherwise DnrInstance::unpackAdn(begin,end) may throw BadValue or InvalidOptionDnrDomainName.
Iterators must be valid for input; passing invalid iterators is undefined.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a heap-allocated copy of this Option6Dnr instance. Use when duplicating options for independent ownership or modification.
requirements: This Option6Dnr instance must be in a valid initialized state before cloning.
Caller must manage the returned OptionPtr appropriately (shared ownership semantics).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::pack
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::pack(util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = false) const override
functions.description: Serializes the option into DHCP wire format and appends it to the provided output buffer. Intended for emitting the full DHCPv6 option 144 on the wire. The check flag is ignored for DHCPv6 (used only in v4). Throws if mandatory fields are invalid.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable OutputBuffer reference.
The mandatory field Authentication Domain Name (ADN) must be non-empty; otherwise InvalidOptionDnrDomainName is thrown.
All internal fields must be consistent and encodable per RFC9463 (e.g., previously parsed/assigned values).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::unpack
functions.description: Parses the provided buffer range as DHCPv6 option 144 payload and populates this Option6Dnr instance. Throws on truncation or if ADN parsing fails.
requirements: begin and end must delimit the complete option payload; data must not be truncated.
ADN data must be valid per DnrInstance parsing; otherwise BadValue or InvalidOptionDnrDomainName may be thrown.
Iterators must be valid for input; passing invalid iterators is undefined.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable textual representation of the option, optionally prefixed with a given number of spaces. Useful for logging and debugging.
requirements: indent should be a non-negative integer; negative values may produce unspecified formatting.
The object should be initialized to produce meaningful output.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::len
functions.description: Returns the total length of the option, including the DHCPv6 option header and the data length. Use to size buffers or validate output lengths.
requirements: The instance must reflect the current internal state; length calculation assumes fields are set consistently.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::packAddresses
functions.description: Appends the stored IP address list to the buffer in wire format for DHCPv6 DNR. Throws if any address is not IPv6.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable isc::util::OutputBuffer reference.
All addresses to be packed must be IPv6; packing a non-IPv6 address will throw BadValue.
The internal address list must be initialized/populated before calling.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6Dnr::unpackAddresses
functions.description: Parses IPv6 address data from the buffer and stores them internally. The function consumes bytes from begin up to end. Throws on malformed data or non-IPv6 addresses.
requirements: begin and end must delimit the available address field data and must be valid input iterators.
Addr Length must be non-zero and divisible by 16; otherwise OutOfRange is thrown.
Address bytes must be present (not truncated) for all addresses; otherwise OutOfRange is thrown.
All parsed addresses must be IPv6; encountering a non-IPv6 address causes BadValue.
On success, begin is advanced past the consumed bytes.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::Option6IA
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv6 IA option (e.g., IA_NA or IA_PD) for transmission, initializing the option with the given type and IAID. Use when creating an option to be packed onto the wire.
requirements: type should be a valid DHCPv6 IA option code (commonly 4 for IA_NA or 25 for IA_PD)
iaid must be a 32-bit value; no additional constraints are specified
Object must be further configured (e.g., T1/T2, suboptions) before packing if needed

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this Option6IA, preserving IAID, T1, T2, and any suboptions. Use when you need a duplicate option instance that can be modified independently.
requirements: Returned OptionPtr must be checked for validity before use if the calling code requires it (no specific failure mode documented)

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::pack
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Option6IA::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes this IA option into DHCPv6 wire format and appends it to the provided OutputBuffer. Includes option header, IAID, T1, T2, and any suboptions. The check parameter controls size checks (notably for v4 options; for v6 this typically has no effect).
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable OutputBuffer reference
Object state must be consistent prior to packing (e.g., IAID/T1/T2 set as intended; suboptions valid)
If check is true, caller should be aware that size checking may be enforced (per library behavior); specifics are not documented here

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::unpack
functions.description: Parses the given buffer range as the IA option’s data and populates this object (IAID, T1, T2, and suboptions). Use on received option payloads.
requirements: begin and end must denote a valid readable range of the option data (first byte of option data through the first byte past the end)
The data range must contain at least 12 bytes (OPTION6_IA_LEN) for IAID, T1, and T2
Iterators must refer to the same underlying buffer and satisfy begin <= end
Caller should handle any exceptions or errors that the implementation may throw on malformed input (not specified here)

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string representation of the option, optionally prefixed with the specified number of spaces. Useful for logging and debugging.
requirements: indent should be a non-negative integer; behavior for negative values is unspecified

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::setT1
functions.description: Sets the T1 timer value for this IA option.
requirements: t1 is a 32-bit value; no additional constraints are specified

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::setT2
functions.description: Sets the T2 timer value for this IA option.
requirements: t2 is a 32-bit value; no additional constraints are specified

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::setIAID
functions.description: Sets the Identity Association Identifier (IAID) for this IA option.
requirements: iaid is a 32-bit value; no additional constraints are specified

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::getIAID
functions.description: Returns the current IAID value.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::getT1
functions.description: Returns the current T1 timer value.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::getT2
functions.description: Returns the current T2 timer value.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IA::len
functions.description: Returns the total length of the option in bytes, including the option header and all suboptions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::Option6IAAddr
functions.signature: Option6IAAddr(uint16_t type, const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& addr, uint32_t preferred, uint32_t valid)
functions.description: Constructs an IA Address (IAADDR) DHCPv6 option for transmission from explicit field values. Throws BadValue if the provided address is not IPv6. The preferred and valid parameters represent address lifetimes in seconds. Use when creating an IAADDR option to be packed onto the wire.
requirements: addr must be an IPv6 address (throws BadValue otherwise).
preferred is the address preferred lifetime in seconds (uint32_t range).
valid is the address valid lifetime in seconds (uint32_t range).
type specifies the DHCP option code for this option; must be appropriate for IAADDR in the calling context (exact numeric value not specified here).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this option as an OptionPtr. Use when duplicating options without sharing state.
requirements: The returned pointer must be managed and eventually released by the caller according to OptionPtr semantics (shared ownership).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::pack
functions.signature: void pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes this IAADDR option into DHCP wire format and appends it to buf. The check flag, when false, allows options larger than 255 bytes for DHCPv4; for DHCPv6 this flag is typically not applicable but is accepted for interface consistency.
requirements: buf must be a valid OutputBuffer ready to receive serialized bytes.
Caller should ensure the object’s fields (address, preferred, valid, and any suboptions if applicable) are set to desired values before packing.
If using in a DHCPv4 context, set check=false to bypass the 255-byte size enforcement; for DHCPv6 this flag has no practical effect.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::unpack
functions.signature: virtual void unpack(OptionBufferConstIter begin, OptionBufferConstIter end)
functions.description: Parses the IAADDR option body from the input byte range [begin, end). Updates the object’s fields from the received data.
requirements: begin and end must specify a valid readable range [begin, end) containing the complete IAADDR option body (excluding the DHCP option header).
The range should be at least the fixed IAADDR length (24 bytes) to be valid; truncated data will result in an error (exception type not explicitly documented here for unpack).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the IAADDR option, optionally prefixed with a number of spaces given by indent. Useful for logging and debugging.
requirements: indent specifies the number of leading spaces; non-negative values are expected (negative behavior is unspecified).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::setAddress
functions.description: Sets the IPv6 address carried by this IAADDR option.
requirements: addr should be an IPv6 address; non-IPv6 is not meaningful for IAADDR (inferred from class semantics).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::setPreferred
functions.description: Sets the preferred lifetime (in seconds) of the IAADDR address.
requirements: pref represents a lifetime in seconds within the range of unsigned int. No additional constraints are documented.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::setValid
functions.description: Sets the valid lifetime (in seconds) of the IAADDR address.
requirements: valid represents a lifetime in seconds within the range of unsigned int. No additional constraints are documented.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::getAddress
functions.description: Returns the IPv6 address currently stored in this IAADDR option by value.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::getPreferred
functions.description: Returns the preferred lifetime (in seconds) currently set for this IAADDR option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::getValid
functions.description: Returns the valid lifetime (in seconds) currently set for this IAADDR option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAAddr::len
functions.description: Returns the total serialized length of this option, including the DHCP option header and the option data.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::Option6IAPrefix
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::Option6IAPrefix(uint16_t type, const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& addr, uint8_t prefix_length, uint32_t preferred, uint32_t valid)
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv6 IAPREFIX option from local values: base IPv6 address (the prefix address), prefix length, preferred lifetime, and valid lifetime. Use this when creating an IAPREFIX to transmit. Prefix bits beyond the prefix_length are not automatically masked here (see class notes).
requirements: prefix_length must be in the range 1..128 (per documentation comment)
addr must be an IPv6 address
preferred is a lifetime in seconds; must be a valid 32-bit unsigned value
valid is a lifetime in seconds; must be a valid 32-bit unsigned value
type must be a valid DHCPv6 option code for an IAPREFIX (typically Option 26), although this header does not enforce or document it
Caller must ensure any non-significant bits beyond prefix_length are consistent if required by application logic (constructor does not mask them)

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this Option6IAPrefix instance as an OptionPtr. Use when duplicating the option for further processing or transmission without altering the original.
requirements: The returned pointer must be managed by the caller according to OptionPtr semantics (shared ownership)
No specific preconditions beyond a valid object state

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::pack
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes the IAPREFIX option into DHCP wire format and appends it to the provided OutputBuffer. Returns via side effect by advancing buf. Throws if the address is not IPv6. The check flag, when false, disables size checks applicable to IPv4 options; it is not generally relevant for DHCPv6.
requirements: addr stored in this option must be IPv6; otherwise BadValue is thrown
buf must be a valid OutputBuffer ready to receive bytes
If check is true, size checks applicable to options are enforced (per Option base behavior)

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::unpack
functions.description: Parses the IAPREFIX option from the given buffer range. During parsing, non-significant bits beyond the prefix length are masked to zero to normalize the prefix representation for comparisons.
requirements: [begin, end) must contain a complete IAPREFIX option payload of at least 25 bytes; otherwise OutOfRange is thrown
Iterators must be valid and readable up to end
Caller should ensure the range corresponds to this option’s data (excluding outer option code/length if that is the calling convention)

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string representation of the IAPREFIX option, optionally prefixed with the specified number of spaces for indentation. Useful for logging and debugging.
requirements: indent should be a non-negative integer (typical usage); behavior for negative values is unspecified in this header

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::setPrefix
functions.description: Sets the base IPv6 prefix address and prefix length carried by this option. This simply assigns the values; it does not perform masking or validation here.
requirements: prefix should be an IPv6 address
length should be an IPv6 prefix length in the range 0..128 (inferred from IPv6 semantics)
Caller is responsible for ensuring any desired masking of non-significant bits; this setter does not mask

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::getLength
functions.description: Returns the stored IPv6 prefix length value for this IAPREFIX option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6IAPrefix::len
functions.description: Returns the total length in bytes of this option when serialized, including the DHCP option header.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::Option6PDExclude
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::Option6PDExclude(const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& delegated_prefix, const uint8_t delegated_prefix_length, const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& excluded_prefix, const uint8_t excluded_prefix_length)
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv6 Prefix Exclude (option 67, RFC 6603) from the given delegated prefix/length and excluded prefix/length. Intended for building an option to send. Computes and stores the subnet ID per RFC 6603 section 4.2. Throws on invalid inputs.
requirements: delegated_prefix must represent a valid IPv6 prefix address.
excluded_prefix must represent a valid IPv6 prefix address.
excluded_prefix_length must be greater than delegated_prefix_length (RFC 6603 semantics).
The common prefix bits of delegated_prefix and excluded_prefix must match for the first delegated_prefix_length bits.
On any violation of the above or invalid prefix values, the constructor throws BadValue.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::Option6PDExclude
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv6 Prefix Exclude option object by parsing option data from the iterator range [begin, end). Typically used when decoding received messages.
requirements: begin and end must form a valid range; begin must not be past end.
The range [begin, end) must contain a complete and well-formed Prefix Exclude option payload as defined by RFC 6603 section 4.2 (length and fields must be consistent).
Parsing errors (e.g., malformed or insufficient data) will cause an exception (type not specified here).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a heap-allocated copy of this option. Use when duplicating options for retransmission or buffering.
requirements: The object must be in a valid constructed/parsed state before cloning.
Caller is responsible for managing the returned OptionPtr.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::pack
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes the option to wire format and appends it to the provided output buffer. The encoding includes the excluded prefix length (in bits) and the IPv6 subnet ID computed per RFC 6603 section 4.2.
requirements: buf must reference a valid, writable isc::util::OutputBuffer.
This instance must be in a valid state (properly constructed or successfully unpacked) before packing.
If check is true, standard size checks are enforced by the underlying implementation; if false, over-255 length checks for v4 are relaxed (not typically relevant for DHCPv6).
Caller should handle any exceptions thrown on serialization failures (e.g., invalid internal state).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::unpack
functions.description: Parses option data from the iterator range [begin, end) and initializes this object’s state accordingly. Expects Prefix Exclude option payload per RFC 6603 section 4.2.
requirements: begin and end must form a valid range; begin must not be past end.
The range [begin, end) must contain a complete and well-formed Prefix Exclude option payload; malformed or truncated input will cause an exception (type not specified here).
Only option data (excluding the DHCPv6 option code/length header) should be provided if that is the convention in the surrounding codebase (per class usage).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::len
functions.description: Returns the total on-the-wire length of this option, including the DHCPv6 option header and the option data.
requirements: Object must be in a valid state; otherwise the returned length may be meaningless or the function may throw depending on implementation.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable textual representation of the option. The output is prefixed by the specified number of spaces.
requirements: indent should be a non-negative integer; behavior for negative values is unspecified.
Object should be in a valid state to produce meaningful output.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::getExcludedPrefix
functions.signature: asiolink::IOAddress isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::getExcludedPrefix(const asiolink::IOAddress& delegated_prefix, const uint8_t delegated_prefix_length) const
functions.description: Computes and returns the excluded IPv6 prefix by combining the provided delegated prefix/length with this option’s stored subnet ID and excluded prefix length, as specified in RFC 6603 section 4.2. Useful when reconstructing the excluded prefix relative to a specific delegated prefix.
requirements: delegated_prefix must be a valid IPv6 prefix address.
delegated_prefix_length must be in the range 0..128 (number of bits for IPv6 prefixes).
This option must contain a valid subnet ID and excluded prefix length (i.e., it must have been constructed or successfully unpacked).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::getExcludedPrefixLength
functions.description: Returns the excluded prefix length (in bits) carried by this option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6PDExclude::getExcludedPrefixSubnetID
functions.description: Returns the stored IPv6 subnet identifier bytes (1..16 octets) as defined by RFC 6603 section 4.2 for the excluded prefix.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as this object remains alive and unmodified.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::Option6StatusCode

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::Option6StatusCode

If the buffer is truncated/insufficient for the fields, constructor throws OutOfRange.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::clone

requirements: buf must be a valid OutputBuffer ready for appending bytes.
Option object must be in a valid state (status code and message set by constructor or setters).
check parameter controls size checking behavior; default is true. No specific exceptions documented here if size constraints are violated.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::unpack
functions.description: Parses the option payload from the provided iterator range and populates this object’s fields. Intended for processing received data.

Throws OutOfRange if the option data is truncated.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::len
functions.description: Returns the total on-the-wire length of this option, including the option header and data fields.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the option, optionally prefixed with a specified number of spaces for indentation. Includes header information plus data.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::dataToText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string of the option’s data only: the status code and status message, excluding the option header.
requirements: Object must be in a valid state; returns a string representation only.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::getStatusCode
functions.description: Accessor returning the numeric DHCPv6 status code value stored in this option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::getStatusCodeName
functions.description: Returns a textual name corresponding to the stored status code (e.g., NoAddrsAvail). Exact mapping depends on implementation; unknown codes may be represented generically.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::setStatusCode
functions.description: Mutator to set or replace the numeric status code value of this option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::getStatusMessage

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option6StatusCode::setStatusMessage

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4SlpServiceScope::len

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Option4SlpServiceScope::getMandatoryFlag
