functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer::getItems
functions.signature:
template<typename ContainerType, typename ItemType, typename Selector>
boost::shared_ptr<ContainerType> isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer<ContainerType, ItemType, Selector>::getItems(const Selector& option_space) const
functions.description: Returns a shared pointer to the container holding items for the specified option space. If there are no items for that option space, a new empty container is returned but is NOT inserted into the option-space map.
requirements: If the returned container corresponds to a non-existent option space, modifications to it will not persist in this OptionSpaceContainer unless the option space is later inserted (e.g., by calling addItem).
Callers should treat the returned container as read-only unless they know the option space already exists in this container.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer::getOptionSpaceNames
functions.signature:
template<typename ContainerType, typename ItemType, typename Selector>
std::list<Selector> isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer<ContainerType, ItemType, Selector>::getOptionSpaceNames() const
functions.description: Returns a list of all selectors (option space names or vendor-ids) currently present in the container. Useful for iterating known option spaces.
requirements: None beyond a properly constructed OptionSpaceContainer instance

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer::clearItems
functions.signature:
template<typename ContainerType, typename ItemType, typename Selector>
void isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer<ContainerType, ItemType, Selector>::clearItems()
functions.description: Removes all option spaces and their items from the container, leaving it empty.
requirements: After calling, all previously returned shared pointers to per-space containers may still point to their containers, but those containers will no longer be reachable via this OptionSpaceContainer.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer::deleteItems
functions.signature:
template<typename ContainerType, typename ItemType, typename Selector>
uint64_t isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer<ContainerType, ItemType, Selector>::deleteItems(const uint64_t id)
functions.description: Deletes all items across all option spaces whose database identifier matches id and returns the number of deleted items. Notes mention that id may be 0 when items were not created by a DB backend; passing 0 removes such items.
requirements: ContainerType must be a Boost.MultiIndex-like container that provides get<OptionIdIndexTag>() returning an index supporting erase(key) by the item identifier type compatible with uint64_t.
ItemType must be indexed by OptionIdIndexTag with a key comparable to id.
Callers may pass any uint64_t; passing 0 is allowed and may delete multiple items as documented.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer::equals
functions.signature:
template<typename ContainerType, typename ItemType, typename Selector>
bool isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer<ContainerType, ItemType, Selector>::equals(const isc::dhcp::OptionSpaceContainer<ContainerType, ItemType, Selector>& other) const
functions.description: Compares two containers for equality. Returns true if they contain the same set of selectors and, for each selector, the same set of items, regardless of order. Uses ItemType::equals to compare items.
requirements: ItemType must provide a method bool equals(const ItemType&) const with semantics suitable for equality comparison.
The comparison is order-insensitive; duplicate handling is determined by ContainerType’s semantics.
other must be an OptionSpaceContainer instantiated with the same template parameters (ContainerType, ItemType, Selector).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionString::OptionString
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::OptionString::OptionString(const isc::dhcp::Option::Universe u, const uint16_t type, const std::string& value)
functions.description: Constructs an OptionString intended for transmission with a single string value. Trailing NULL characters in the provided value are trimmed. Throws if the string is empty.
requirements: u must be a valid universe value (isc::dhcp::Option::V4 or isc::dhcp::Option::V6).
type is the DHCP option code appropriate for the chosen universe.
value must be a non-empty string; otherwise isc::OutOfRange is thrown.
Trailing NULL characters in value are removed before storage.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionString::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this OptionString as a polymorphic OptionPtr. Use when duplicating options for modification or reuse without affecting the original.
requirements: The source object must be in a valid state (constructed or successfully unpacked) before cloning.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionString::len
functions.description: Returns the total on-wire length of the option including its header (code and length for v4 or option header for v6). Useful for pre-sizing buffers or validation.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionString::getValue
functions.description: Returns the string value carried by this option. The stored value has any trailing NULLs removed.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionString::setValue
functions.description: Sets/replaces the string value carried by this option. Trailing NULLs in the input are trimmed. Throws if the provided string is empty.
requirements: value must be a non-empty string; otherwise isc::OutOfRange is thrown.
Trailing NULL characters in value are removed before storage.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionString::pack
functions.signature: virtual void isc::dhcp::OptionString::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Encodes this option into on-wire format and appends it to the provided output buffer. The buffer's write position advances to the end of the appended data. For DHCPv4, setting check to false allows options larger than 255 bytes.
requirements: buf must be a valid isc::util::OutputBuffer capable of appending data.
Call only on an OptionString that has a valid value set (constructed or setValue called).
If targeting DHCPv4 and the encoded option would exceed 255 bytes, callers may set check=false to bypass size checks (behavior with check=true is implementation-defined in this header).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionString::unpack
functions.description: Decodes the option payload from the given buffer range into this OptionString. The range must contain only the payload (not the option code and length). The payload size must be at least 1 byte. Trailing NULL bytes are trimmed. Throws if the buffer is truncated.
requirements: [begin, end) must point to the option payload only; do not include option code or length.
The payload size must be at least 1 byte; otherwise isc::OutOfRange is thrown.
begin and end must be valid iterators such that begin <= end and refer to accessible memory.
Trailing NULL bytes in the payload will be removed during unpacking.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionString::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable textual representation of the option, prefixed by the given number of space characters for indentation.
requirements: indent specifies the number of leading spaces; behavior for negative values is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionString::toString
functions.description: Returns the actual string value of the option for use in contexts such as client classification.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionVendor::OptionVendor
functions.description: Constructs a vendor-specific information option (RFC 3925) for the given DHCP universe (V4 or V6) with the specified enterprise identifier. Use when creating an OptionVendor programmatically prior to adding it to a packet or an option collection.
requirements: u must be a valid isc::dhcp::Option::Universe value (V4 or V6).
vendor_id is a 32-bit enterprise identifier; typical usage is an IANA Enterprise Number (inferred from name and comments).
Object must be further populated (e.g., with suboptions) as needed before packing to wire format (inferred from class purpose).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionVendor::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this OptionVendor as an OptionPtr. Use when duplicating options before modification or insertion into different containers.
requirements: The source object must be in a valid state prior to cloning (inferred from typical clone semantics).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionVendor::pack
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::OptionVendor::pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const
functions.description: Serializes this vendor-specific option into DHCP wire format and appends it to the provided OutputBuffer. For DHCPv4, if check is false, options larger than 255 bytes are allowed.
requirements: buf must be a valid isc::util::OutputBuffer instance ready to receive data.

When targeting DHCPv4 and check is true (default), the caller should ensure the encoded option size does not exceed 255 bytes; setting check to false allows larger-than-255 v4 options as noted in the comment.
The object must have been correctly initialized (e.g., vendor id set; suboptions added as needed) before packing (inferred from purpose).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionVendor::unpack
functions.description: Parses the vendor-specific option from the given [begin, end) buffer range and populates this object. On parsing errors it throws isc::SkipRemainingOptionsBuffer to indicate remaining options cannot be parsed but the packet may still be processed.
requirements: begin and end must define a valid range of bytes containing the option payload; begin must not be past end.
The iterators must remain valid for the duration of the call and refer to a contiguous memory block.
Caller should be prepared to handle isc::SkipRemainingOptionsBuffer on parsing errors as documented.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionVendor::setVendorId
functions.description: Sets the enterprise identifier (vendor-id) carried by this option.
requirements: vendor_id must be a 32-bit value. Typical usage is to supply a valid IANA Enterprise Number (inferred from comments).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionVendor::getVendorId
functions.description: Returns the current enterprise identifier (vendor-id) stored in this option.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionVendor::len
functions.description: Computes and returns the total on-the-wire length of this option, including option header and all suboptions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::OptionVendor::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable textual representation of this vendor-specific option. The indent parameter specifies the number of leading spaces to prepend to the text.
requirements: indent is an integer; typical usage is non-negative values to increase readability (inferred).

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::OptionVendorClass
functions.description: Constructs a DHCP Vendor Class option for the specified universe (DHCPv4 V-I Vendor Class or DHCPv6 Vendor Class) with the given enterprise/vendor ID. For v4, the constructor inserts one empty opaque-data tuple to satisfy RFC3925’s requirement that at least one data-length field be present; for v6, no tuple is added by default. Use this when creating a new option programmatically for a known enterprise ID.
requirements: u must be either Option::V4 or Option::V6.
vendor_id should be a valid enterprise (vendor) identifier encoded as a 32-bit integer; specific value constraints are not enforced here.
For v4, the option must contain at least one data-length field; the constructor ensures an empty tuple exists by default (no additional caller action required).

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::OptionVendorClass
functions.signature: OptionVendorClass(Option::Universe u, OptionBufferConstIter begin, OptionBufferConstIter end);
functions.description: Constructs a Vendor Class option by parsing on-wire data from the iterator range [begin, end). The universe determines whether the data is interpreted as DHCPv4 V-I Vendor Class (option 124) or DHCPv6 Vendor Class (option 16). This may throw if unpack() detects malformed or inconsistent data. Use this to decode received options.
requirements: u must be either Option::V4 or Option::V6.
begin and end must delimit a valid buffer containing exactly one Vendor Class option payload appropriate for the specified universe.
The buffer must be at least the minimal option length (6 bytes for v4, 8 bytes for v6) and otherwise well-formed; otherwise an exception may be thrown by unpack().

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this OptionVendorClass instance as an OptionPtr. Use when duplicating the option for later modification or independent ownership.
requirements: The source object must be in a valid state (i.e., previously constructed and not destroyed).
Caller assumes ownership of the returned OptionPtr and should manage its lifetime accordingly.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::pack
functions.signature: virtual void pack(isc::util::OutputBuffer& buf, bool check = true) const;
functions.description: Serializes the option into wire format and appends it to the provided OutputBuffer. If check is true, standard size limits are enforced (notably the 255-byte length limit for DHCPv4 options); if false, larger-than-255-byte v4 options are allowed. Use this before sending an option on the wire.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable isc::util::OutputBuffer instance.
If getUniverse() == Option::V4 and check == true, the encoded option length must not exceed 255 bytes, otherwise an exception may be thrown.
All tuples contained must be compatible with the option’s universe (v4 vs v6), or packing may fail.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::unpack
functions.signature: virtual void unpack(OptionBufferConstIter begin, OptionBufferConstIter end);
functions.description: Parses on-wire data from [begin, end) to populate the enterprise ID and the collection of opaque-data tuples. Throws on malformed data, invalid lengths, or tuples inconsistent with the universe.
requirements: begin and end must define a valid contiguous buffer range.
The input data must be at least the minimal length for the selected universe (6 bytes for v4, 8 bytes for v6) and must conform to the RFC-defined encoding for that universe.
Tuples in the data must be of a type compatible with the option’s universe; otherwise an exception is thrown.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::getVendorId
functions.description: Returns the enterprise (vendor) ID associated with this option. Useful for identifying the vendor for which the tuples are intended.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::addTuple
functions.description: Appends an opaque-data tuple to the option. Throws isc::BadValue if the tuple type does not match the option’s universe (v4 vs v6). Use to add additional vendor-class data entries.
requirements: tuple must be of a type compatible with the option’s universe; otherwise isc::BadValue is thrown.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::setTuple
functions.signature: void setTuple(const size_t at, const OpaqueDataTuple& tuple);
functions.description: Replaces the tuple at index 'at' with the provided tuple. Throws isc::OutOfRange if the index is invalid and isc::BadValue if the tuple type is incompatible with the universe.
requirements: at must be less than getTuplesNum(); otherwise isc::OutOfRange is thrown.
tuple must be of a type compatible with the option’s universe; otherwise isc::BadValue is thrown.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::getTuple
functions.description: Returns a copy of the tuple at the specified index. Throws isc::OutOfRange if the index is invalid.
requirements: at must be less than getTuplesNum(); otherwise isc::OutOfRange is thrown.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::getTuplesNum
functions.description: Returns the number of opaque-data tuples currently stored in this option.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::getTuples
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the collection of opaque-data tuples carried by this option. Use for read-only iteration without copying.
requirements: The returned reference is read-only; callers must not attempt to modify the collection.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::hasTuple
functions.description: Checks whether any contained tuple matches the provided string representation. Returns true if a matching tuple exists. Intended for quick presence checks by string value.
requirements: tuple_str must be a string representation comparable to how OpaqueDataTuple produces or interprets string values; exact matching semantics beyond string equality are not specified.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::len
functions.description: Returns the total on-wire length of the option including its header. Useful for sizing buffers and validating option sizes prior to packing.

functions.name: OptionVendorClass::toText
functions.description: Returns a human-readable textual representation of the option, optionally prefixed with 'indent' spaces. Useful for logging and debugging.
requirements: indent is used as a count of leading spaces; specific bounds are not documented.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::InvalidQueueParameter::InvalidQueueParameter
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::InvalidQueueParameter::InvalidQueueParameter(const char* file, size_t line, const char* what)
functions.description: Constructs an InvalidQueueParameter exception describing an invalid or missing parameter supplied to a packet queue. Typical usage is to throw this from queue implementations or factories when configuration/arguments are invalid.
requirements: file must point to a valid, null-terminated C string identifying the source file
what must point to a valid, null-terminated C string describing the error
line should be the source code line number associated with the error (non-negative)

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::PacketQueue
functions.description: Constructs the abstract packet queue interface with a logical queue implementation name. Intended to be invoked by concrete queue implementations (e.g., from a factory) to record the queue type used for reporting/inspection.
requirements: Must be called by/for a concrete PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr> implementation; PacketQueue is an abstract interface
queue_type should be a meaningful logical name of the queue implementation; exact format/values are not specified

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::~PacketQueue
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the abstract packet queue interface, enabling safe destruction via base-class pointers.
requirements: The object must be a valid PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr> instance (typically a concrete derived class) when destroyed

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::enqueuePacket
functions.signature: template <typename PacketTypePtr> virtual void isc::dhcp::PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr>::enqueuePacket(PacketTypePtr packet, const isc::dhcp::SocketInfo& source) = 0
functions.description: Enqueue a DHCP packet into the queue, recording the socket it arrived on. Concrete implementations decide which packets are accepted and how they are queued.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr> implementation (pure virtual)
packet must be of the correct pointer type (e.g., Pkt4Ptr or Pkt6Ptr depending on the instantiation)
source must reference a valid isc::dhcp::SocketInfo describing the packet’s source socket
Thread-safety is provided by implementations; no special synchronization is required by the caller unless specified by a particular implementation

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::dequeuePacket
functions.description: Dequeue and return the next packet from the queue. If the queue is empty, returns an empty pointer. The dequeue policy/order is implementation-defined.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr> implementation (pure virtual)
Caller must handle the possibility of an empty (null) return when the queue is empty

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::empty
functions.description: Returns true if the queue currently holds no packets.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr> implementation (pure virtual)

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::getSize
functions.description: Returns the current number of packets stored in the queue.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr> implementation (pure virtual)

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::clear
functions.description: Removes all packets from the queue.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr> implementation (pure virtual)
Caller should be prepared for all queued packets to be discarded

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::getInfo
functions.description: Returns an ElementPtr (JSON-like structure) of operational information for the queue. The base implementation provides a map with a single entry "queue-type" set to the logical queue type. Derived implementations typically call this first and then add additional fields.
requirements: May be called on any PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr> instance (base provides a default implementation)
Returned ElementPtr will at least contain key "queue-type" as a string

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::getInfoStr
functions.description: Returns a JSON string representation of the operational info by invoking getInfo() and serializing its contents.
requirements: Caller should be prepared to receive valid JSON text corresponding to the Element returned by getInfo()

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueue::getQueueType
functions.description: Returns the logical name (type) of this queue implementation as provided at construction. Useful for diagnostics and introspection.
requirements: None beyond having a valid PacketQueue<PacketTypePtr> instance

functions.name: isc::dhcp::InvalidQueueType::InvalidQueueType
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::InvalidQueueType::InvalidQueueType(const char* file, size_t line, const char* what)
functions.description: Constructs an InvalidQueueType exception indicating the packet queue type is not recognized. Typical usage is to throw this when a requested queue type is not registered. Parameters identify the source file, line, and message.
requirements: file must be a valid C-string pointer or nullptr-safe string literal used for diagnostics.
line should be the source line number where the exception is created.
what must describe the error condition; it is stored for later retrieval via what().
Callers should be prepared to catch this exception when creating or configuring packet queues.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr::PacketQueueMgr
functions.description: Default-constructs a PacketQueueMgr instance with an empty registry of factories and no current packet queue. Use this manager to register queue factories and to create/destroy/access the active packet queue.
requirements: PacketQueueTypePtr must be a pointer-like type to a packet queue interface compatible with isc::dhcp::PacketQueue (e.g. PacketQueue4Ptr/PacketQueue6Ptr).
No other preconditions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr::registerPacketQueueFactory
functions.signature:
template<typename PacketQueueTypePtr>
bool isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr<PacketQueueTypePtr>::registerPacketQueueFactory(const std::string& queue_type, std::function<PacketQueueTypePtr(isc::data::ConstElementPtr)> factory)
functions.description: Registers a factory function under the specified queue type string so the manager can later create that type of packet queue from configuration. Returns true on success, or false if a factory for that queue_type is already registered. Typical usage is in a hooks library load routine to make a queue implementation available.
requirements: queue_type identifies the queue implementation (e.g. "kea-ring4"); it must be unique within this manager instance.
factory must be a callable that, when invoked with the configuration (isc::data::ConstElementPtr), returns a non-null PacketQueueTypePtr or throws on error.
If a factory is already registered for queue_type, the function returns false and leaves existing registration intact.
No validation of factory is performed at registration time; misuse may lead to exceptions when creating a queue.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr::unregisterPacketQueueFactory
functions.description: Unregisters the factory associated with the given queue_type. If the currently active packet queue is of that type, it is destroyed to avoid leaving an instance whose code may be unloaded. Returns true if a factory was removed, false if no factory was registered for that type.
requirements: queue_type must match an existing registration to have any effect; otherwise the function returns false.
If the currently active queue's type equals queue_type, it will be reset (destroyed), discarding any queued packets.
Callers should be aware that removing a factory prevents subsequent creation of that queue type until it is re-registered.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr::createPacketQueue
functions.description: Creates a new packet queue instance based on the given configuration and makes it the current queue. The configuration must specify "queue-type" (string), which is used to find a registered factory. The factory is invoked with the parameters to construct the queue. On success, the existing queue (if any) is replaced; on failure, the existing queue is left unchanged. Exceptions are thrown for invalid parameters, unsupported type, or null factory result.
requirements: parameters must be non-null.
parameters must be a map-like element containing a string field "queue-type" parsable by isc::data::SimpleParser::getString.
A factory for the specified queue-type must have been previously registered; otherwise InvalidQueueType is thrown.
Factories are expected to throw InvalidQueueParameter on bad configuration; callers should be prepared to catch exceptions (InvalidQueueParameter, InvalidQueueType, Unexpected).
Factories must return a non-null PacketQueueTypePtr; otherwise an Unexpected exception is thrown.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr::getPacketQueue
functions.description: Returns the current packet queue instance managed by this PacketQueueMgr. May be null if no queue has been created or if it was destroyed/unregistered.
requirements: Callers must handle the possibility of a null return (no active queue).
No other preconditions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr::destroyPacketQueue
functions.description: Destroys (resets) the current packet queue instance. Any queued packets will be discarded. After this call, getPacketQueue() will return null until a new queue is created.
requirements: Callers should understand that queued packets are lost upon destruction.
Safe to call when no queue is active; it becomes a no-op.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr4::PacketQueueMgr4
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv4 packet queue manager. On construction, it registers the default factory for DHCPv4 packet queues and prepares management of the current queue instance. Use this to initialize queue handling for a DHCPv4 server.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr4::~PacketQueueMgr4
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the DHCPv4 packet queue manager. It enables proper cleanup via base-class pointers; no special teardown behavior is defined in the header.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr6::PacketQueueMgr6
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv6 packet queue manager. On construction it registers the default factory for DHCPv6 packet queues so the manager can create/manage the default queue implementation. Typical usage is to instantiate this manager at server startup and then use the PacketQueueMgr<PacketQueue6Ptr> interface (from the base class) to access or configure the active queue.
requirements: The class is non-copyable (inherits from boost::noncopyable); callers must not attempt to copy or assign instances.
No arguments are required; there are no explicit preconditions documented for construction.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueMgr6::~PacketQueueMgr6
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the DHCPv6 packet queue manager. It allows safe deletion via base-class pointers and ensures proper cleanup of any resources owned by the manager. The header defines it as an inline empty destructor.
requirements: Destruction should occur when the manager is no longer in use; callers must not access the object after it has been destroyed.
The class is non-copyable; object ownership should be managed appropriately (e.g., via PacketQueueMgr6Ptr) to avoid multiple deletions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::PacketQueueRing
functions.signature:
template<typename PacketTypePtr>
isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing<PacketTypePtr>::PacketQueueRing(const std::string& queue_type, size_t capacity)
functions.description: Constructor for a ring-buffer implementation of PacketQueue. Initializes the underlying circular buffer with the given capacity and allocates an internal mutex. Intended to be used to create a queue for PacketTypePtr (e.g., Pkt4Ptr or Pkt6Ptr).
requirements: queue_type is a logical identifier only; no constraints enforced by this constructor.
capacity is passed directly to the internal circular buffer; no minimum is enforced here (setCapacity enforces a minimum if used).
Thread-safety: construction must occur before the instance is shared across threads.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::~PacketQueueRing
functions.description: Virtual destructor for PacketQueueRing. Cleans up resources (notably the mutex and container) when the queue is destroyed.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
Ensure no other threads are operating on the queue during destruction.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::enqueuePacket
functions.signature:
template<typename PacketTypePtr>
virtual void isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing<PacketTypePtr>::enqueuePacket(PacketTypePtr packet, const SocketInfo& source)
functions.description: Enqueue a packet at the back of the queue unless shouldDropPacket(packet, source) returns true. Default behavior is to accept all packets (shouldDropPacket returns false).
requirements: May be called concurrently; the underlying push operation is internally synchronized.
PacketTypePtr may be empty; no validation is performed.
Behavior of acceptance/dropping may differ if shouldDropPacket is overridden in a derived class.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::dequeuePacket
functions.description: Dequeues and returns the next packet from the front of the queue after first allowing a derived class to discard packets via eatPackets(QueueEnd::FRONT). Returns an empty pointer if the queue is empty.
requirements: May be called concurrently; pop operation is internally synchronized.
If a derived class overrides eatPackets, its semantics determine which packets are skipped before dequeue.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::shouldDropPacket
functions.signature:
template<typename PacketTypePtr>
virtual bool isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing<PacketTypePtr>::shouldDropPacket(PacketTypePtr packet, const SocketInfo& source)
functions.description: Hook to decide whether a packet should be dropped at enqueue time. Default implementation always returns false (keep the packet). Derived classes can inspect the packet and source and override this decision. Note: packet is not unpacked at this stage.
requirements: No specific requirements on packet or source; default implementation ignores them.
If overridden, callers should expect that packets may be dropped based on custom policy.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::eatPackets
functions.signature:
template<typename PacketTypePtr>
virtual int isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing<PacketTypePtr>::eatPackets(const QueueEnd& from)
functions.description: Hook invoked before dequeue to optionally discard packets from one end of the queue (typically the front). Default implementation discards none and returns 0. Derived classes may implement custom skipping logic.
requirements: Parameter from should be a valid QueueEnd value (e.g., QueueEnd::FRONT or QueueEnd::BACK).
If overridden in derived classes, callers should be aware that packets may be skipped before dequeue.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::pushPacket
functions.signature:
template<typename PacketTypePtr>
virtual void isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing<PacketTypePtr>::pushPacket(PacketTypePtr& packet, const QueueEnd& to = QueueEnd::BACK)
functions.description: Pushes a packet onto the specified end of the queue (back by default). Operation is protected by an internal mutex.
requirements: Parameter to must be a valid QueueEnd value (QueueEnd::BACK or QueueEnd::FRONT).
May be called concurrently; function is internally synchronized.
packet may be an empty pointer; no validation or null-check is enforced.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::popPacket
functions.signature:
template<typename PacketTypePtr>
virtual PacketTypePtr isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing<PacketTypePtr>::popPacket(const QueueEnd& from = QueueEnd::FRONT)
functions.description: Pops and returns a packet from the specified end of the queue (front by default). Returns an empty pointer if the queue is empty. Operation is protected by an internal mutex.
requirements: Parameter from must be a valid QueueEnd value (QueueEnd::FRONT or QueueEnd::BACK).
May be called concurrently; function is internally synchronized.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::peek
functions.signature:
template<typename PacketTypePtr>
virtual const PacketTypePtr isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing<PacketTypePtr>::peek(const QueueEnd& from = QueueEnd::FRONT) const
functions.description: Returns (without removing) the packet at the specified end of the queue (front by default). Returns an empty pointer if the queue is empty. Note: this method does not lock the internal mutex.
requirements: Parameter from must be a valid QueueEnd value (QueueEnd::FRONT or QueueEnd::BACK).
Not internally synchronized; if used in a multithreaded context, callers must externally synchronize to avoid races with mutating operations.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::empty
functions.description: Returns true if the queue is empty, false otherwise. This method acquires the internal mutex.
requirements: May be called concurrently; function is internally synchronized.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::getCapacity
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of packets allowed in the underlying buffer (circular buffer capacity).
requirements: Not internally synchronized; in multithreaded usage, callers should externally synchronize if other threads may modify the queue or its capacity concurrently.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::setCapacity
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of packets allowed in the buffer. Throws BadValue if capacity is below MIN_RING_CAPACITY (5).
requirements: capacity must be >= MIN_RING_CAPACITY (5) or the function throws BadValue.
Changing capacity while other threads are operating on the queue is not synchronized by this method; callers must ensure external synchronization if used concurrently.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::getSize
functions.description: Returns the current number of packets in the buffer.
requirements: Not internally synchronized; in multithreaded usage, callers should externally synchronize if other threads may modify the queue concurrently.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::clear
functions.description: Discards all packets currently in the buffer by clearing the underlying container.
requirements: Not internally synchronized; callers must ensure no concurrent operations are accessing the queue when calling clear, or externally synchronize.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing::getInfo
functions.description: Returns a data::Element structure containing runtime information about the queue (at least 'capacity' and 'size'), augmenting the base PacketQueue::getInfo() output.
requirements: Relies on getCapacity() and getSize(), which are not internally synchronized; for multithreaded use, callers should externally synchronize if concurrent modification is possible.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing4::PacketQueueRing4
functions.description: Constructor for a DHCPv4 packet ring queue. Initializes the base PacketQueueRing with the provided type name and capacity.
requirements: Same as the base constructor: capacity is applied to the underlying buffer without minimum enforcement here.
Construct before publishing to other threads.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing4::~PacketQueueRing4
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the DHCPv4 ring queue.
requirements: Ensure no other threads are using the queue during destruction.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing6::PacketQueueRing6
functions.description: Constructor for a DHCPv6 packet ring queue. Initializes the base PacketQueueRing with the provided type name and capacity.
requirements: Same as the base constructor: capacity is applied to the underlying buffer without minimum enforcement here.
Construct before publishing to other threads.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PacketQueueRing6::~PacketQueueRing6
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the DHCPv6 ring queue.
requirements: Ensure no other threads are using the queue during destruction.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::ScopedEnableOptionsCopy<PktType>::ScopedEnableOptionsCopy
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::ScopedEnableOptionsCopy<PktType>::ScopedEnableOptionsCopy(const boost::shared_ptr<PktType>& pkt1, const boost::shared_ptr<PktType>& pkt2 = boost::shared_ptr<PktType>())

functions.description: RAII destructor that disables copying of retrieved options on the managed packets, restoring their prior behavior when the scope ends.
requirements: Only guarantees to call setCopyRetrievedOptions(false) on non-null stored packet pointers.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktEvent::PktEvent
functions.description: Constructs a packet event record with a label and timestamp (expected UTC with microsecond precision). Used to track packet lifecycle milestones for diagnostics.
requirements: label is an arbitrary identifier string.
timestamp should represent UTC/microseconds as per comments.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktEvent::~PktEvent
functions.description: Default destructor for PktEvent. No special behavior.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktEvent::now
functions.description: Returns the current UTC system time with microsecond precision. Convenience for timestamping events.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktEvent::EMPTY_TIME
functions.description: Returns a reference to a static, unset ptime used as an empty timestamp sentinel for comparisons.
requirements: The returned reference refers to a static object; do not store pointers beyond typical use.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktEvent::MIN_TIME
functions.description: Returns a reference to the minimum timestamp value.
requirements: The returned reference refers to a static object; do not attempt to modify it globally.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktEvent::MAX_TIME
functions.description: Returns a reference to the maximum timestamp value.
requirements: The returned reference refers to a static object; do not attempt to modify it globally.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::pack
functions.description: Pure virtual. Prepare the packet (DHCPv4 or DHCPv6) and all options into on-wire format and write to buffer_out_. Implemented by derived classes (e.g. Pkt4, Pkt6).
requirements: Caller should ensure options_ contains the options to encode before calling.
Valid only for TX packets; RX packets typically use unpack().
Derived implementations should clear buffer_out_ before writing.
Throws InvalidOperation on packing failure (per comments).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::unpack
functions.description: Pure virtual. Parse on-wire data in data_ into options_ and packet fields. Implemented by derived classes (e.g. Pkt4, Pkt6).
requirements: Caller must ensure data_ holds the received on-wire bytes and that the object represents an RX packet.
Throws on parse failure (type unspecified in header).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getBuffer
functions.description: Returns a reference to the packet's output buffer. For TX packets after pack(), the buffer contains the on-wire data; otherwise it may be empty.
requirements: Only valid for the lifetime of the packet object.
For RX packets or TX packets before pack(), returned buffer length may be zero.
Hooks/callouts may modify the returned buffer.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::addOption
functions.description: Adds an option to the packet's options_ collection. Derived classes may enforce uniqueness or other rules (e.g., Pkt4).
requirements: opt should refer to a valid Option instance; behavior for null is unspecified in header.
Call after unpack() for RX or before pack() for TX, depending on use.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::delOption
functions.description: Deletes the first option of the specified type from options_, if present.
requirements: type is a DHCP option code. No range is explicitly enforced in the header.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getLabel
functions.description: Returns a human-readable identifier for the packet for logging. Base implementation throws NotImplemented; derived classes should override.
requirements: Caller should expect an exception from the base class unless calling a derived override.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::toText
functions.signature: virtual std::string isc::dhcp::Pkt::toText(bool verbose = false) const
functions.description: Pure virtual. Returns a string dump of the packet for debugging; when verbose is true, includes most members and extra detail.
requirements: Implemented in derived classes (e.g., Pkt4, Pkt6).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::len
functions.description: Pure virtual. Returns the size in bytes of the packet in on-wire format (or required to store it).
requirements: Implemented in derived classes.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getType
functions.description: Pure virtual. Returns the DHCP message type (e.g., SOLICIT=1 for DHCPv6).
requirements: Implemented in derived classes.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setType
functions.description: Pure virtual. Sets the DHCP message type field.
requirements: Implemented in derived classes.
type must be a valid message type for the corresponding protocol (not enforced here).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getName
functions.description: Pure virtual. Returns the canonical name for the DHCP message type, or "UNKNOWN" for unsupported types. Should return a statically allocated string.
requirements: Implemented in derived classes.
Returned pointer must not be freed by caller.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setTransid
functions.description: Sets the packet's transaction ID value (32-bit for v4, 24-bit for v6 stored in 32 bits).
requirements: transid is stored as given; protocol-specific width constraints are handled by derived uses.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getTransid
functions.description: Returns the packet's transaction ID value.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::inClass
functions.description: Checks if the packet is a member of the specified client class.
requirements: client_class identifies the class to check.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::addClass
functions.description: Adds the specified client class to the packet's class set. Re-adding the same class is silently ignored.
requirements: client_class is the name/identifier of the class to add.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::addAdditionalClass
functions.description: Adds a class to the packet's additional-classes list for later evaluation during additional class processing. Re-adding is silently ignored.
requirements: client_class is the name/identifier of the class to add.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::addSubClass
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Pkt::addSubClass(const isc::dhcp::ClientClass& class_def, const isc::dhcp::ClientClass& subclass)
functions.description: Adds a subclass relationship (class definition and subclass) to the packet.
requirements: class_def identifies the class definition.
subclass identifies the subclass to associate.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getClasses
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the set of classes the packet belongs to. Intended for iteration only.
requirements: Do not modify the returned collection (const reference).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getAdditionalClasses
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the list of additional classes pending evaluation.
requirements: Intended for iteration only; do not modify.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getSubClassesRelations
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the list of subclass relationships (template classes associated with subclasses).
requirements: Intended for iteration only; do not modify.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::cloneOptions
functions.description: Creates and returns a container of deep-cloned options so they can be safely modified without affecting originals.
requirements: Call after unpack() if cloning received options; otherwise ensure options_ is populated.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getOption
functions.description: Returns the first option of the specified type. If copying of retrieved options is enabled, returns a copied option and replaces original in the packet with the copy.
requirements: Packet must have been unpacked (for RX) before retrieval to populate options_.
type is the option code to search for.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getOptions
functions.description: Returns all option instances of the specified type. In DHCPv6, multiple instances may exist.
requirements: type is the option code to search for.
If copy_retrieved_options_ is enabled, options may be copied before being returned (per class behavior).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setCopyRetrievedOptions
functions.description: Enables or disables copying of options when retrieved via getOption/getOptions. When enabled, the returned option is a copy and replaces the original in the packet to prevent unintended external modification of shared Option instances.
requirements: Set true before passing packet to hook libraries if you need defensive copies.
Affects subsequent getOption/getOptions calls.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::isCopyRetrievedOptions
functions.description: Returns whether copying of retrieved options is currently enabled.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::updateTimestamp
functions.description: Updates the packet timestamp (typically just before sending or just after receiving).
requirements: May throw isc::Unexpected if timestamp update fails.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getTimestamp
functions.description: Returns the packet's timestamp last updated by updateTimestamp() or explicitly set.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setTimestamp
functions.description: Sets the packet's timestamp to the provided value.
requirements: timestamp should be UTC/microseconds per convention.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::addPktEvent
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Pkt::addPktEvent(const std::string& label, const boost::posix_time::ptime& timestamp = isc::dhcp::PktEvent::now())
functions.description: Appends an event with the given label and timestamp (defaults to now) to the packet's event stack.
requirements: label identifies the event logically.
timestamp is expected UTC/microseconds.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setPktEvent
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Pkt::setPktEvent(const std::string& label, const boost::posix_time::ptime& timestamp = isc::dhcp::PktEvent::now())
functions.description: Updates the timestamp of an existing event with the given label, or adds it if missing. Intended mainly for tests.
requirements: label identifies the event to update.
timestamp is expected UTC/microseconds.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::clearPktEvents
functions.description: Clears the packet's event stack. Provided primarily for tests.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getPktEventTime
functions.description: Returns the timestamp of the event with the given label from the event stack.
requirements: label must match an event previously added; behavior if missing is not specified here.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getPktEvents
functions.description: Returns a reference to the current list of packet events.
requirements: Returned reference is valid only as long as the packet exists.
Do not assume thread-safety.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::dumpPktEvents
functions.description: Returns a textual dump of the packet's event stack suitable for logging. If verbose, includes durations between events and spans multiple lines.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::repack
functions.description: Copies the current input buffer (data_) into the output buffer (buffer_out_). Used mainly to retransmit a received packet as-is for diagnostics/testing.
requirements: Use when wanting to send a received packet without re-packing.
Ensure data_ contains the intended bytes before calling.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setRemoteAddr
functions.description: Sets the remote IP address (source for RX, destination for TX).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getRemoteAddr
functions.description: Returns the remote IP address.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setLocalAddr
functions.description: Sets the local IP address (destination for RX, source for TX).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getLocalAddr
functions.description: Returns the local IP address.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setLocalPort

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getLocalPort

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setRemotePort
functions.description: Sets the remote UDP/TCP port (source for RX or destination for TX).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getRemotePort
functions.description: Returns the remote UDP/TCP port.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setIndex
functions.description: Sets the interface index on which the packet was or will be sent/received.
requirements: ifindex must be a valid system interface index value.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::resetIndex
functions.description: Resets the interface index to the unset sentinel value (UNSET_IFINDEX).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getIndex
functions.description: Returns the interface index (or UNSET_IFINDEX when not set).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::indexSet
functions.description: Returns true if the interface index has been set (not equal to UNSET_IFINDEX).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getIface
functions.description: Returns the interface name used for RX/TX of the packet.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::setIface
functions.description: Sets the interface name used for RX/TX of the packet.
requirements: iface should be a valid system interface name.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt::getRemoteHWAddr

functions.description: Virtual destructor for Pkt to ensure proper cleanup via base pointers.

requirements: pkt_ reference must still be valid at destruction.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::Pkt4

client_id may be NULL (explicit).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::getHops

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::getYiaddr

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::setYiaddr

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::getGiaddr
functions.description: Return the giaddr (gateway/relay agent IP address) field.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::setGiaddr
