functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::setLocalHWAddr
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::Pkt4::setLocalHWAddr(const uint8_t htype, const uint8_t hlen, const std::vector<uint8_t>& mac_addr)
functions.description: Set the local hardware address (source for outgoing packets or destination for incoming packets) by copying from the provided buffer.
requirements: mac_addr must contain at least hlen bytes (explicit).
htype is the hardware type; hlen is the length (up to 16, inferred from MAX_CHADDR_LEN).
May throw OutOfRange if an invalid HW address is specified (via internal validation; explicit in helper).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::setLocalHWAddr
functions.description: Set the local hardware address from an existing HWAddr structure (source for outgoing, destination for incoming).
requirements: addr must not be null; throws BadValue if addr is null (explicit).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::getLocalHWAddr
functions.description: Return the local hardware address (dst for received packets, src for sent packets).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::getDeferredOptions
functions.description: Return a reference to the list of option codes whose unpacking is deferred. Options 43 and 224–254 are deferred and initially unpacked as unknown options; their codes are recorded here.
requirements: Returned reference is mutable; callers must ensure any modifications respect the intended use (inferred).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::isRelayed
functions.description: Return true if the message is considered relayed, i.e., if giaddr is non-zero and non-broadcast; otherwise false.
requirements: No preconditions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4::isDhcp4o6
functions.description: Return whether the message has been transported over DHCPv6 (DHCPv4-over-DHCPv6). The base Pkt4 implementation always returns false.
requirements: No preconditions.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4o6::Pkt4o6
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::Pkt4o6::Pkt4o6(const isc::dhcp::OptionBuffer& pkt4, const isc::dhcp::Pkt6Ptr& pkt6)
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv4-over-DHCPv6 packet for a received message. The pkt4 argument is the content of the DHCPv4-message option (RFC 7341) extracted from the encapsulating DHCPv6 message; pkt6 is the encapsulating, already-unpacked DHCPv6 message. On construction, the DHCPv4-message option will be removed from pkt6. Use when parsing incoming DHCPv4o6 traffic.
requirements: pkt6 must reference the encapsulating DHCPv6 message corresponding to this DHCPv4 payload.
pkt6 should be in an unpacked state prior to construction (as stated in the comment).
pkt4 must contain a valid DHCPv4 message payload suitable for the DHCPv4-message option as defined by RFC 7341.
Caller should not assume the DHCPv4-message option remains in pkt6 after construction; it will be removed.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4o6::getPkt6
functions.description: Returns the encapsulating DHCPv6 message associated with this DHCPv4-over-DHCPv6 packet. Useful for accessing or modifying DHCPv6 headers/options alongside the embedded DHCPv4 message.
requirements: May return a non-null shared pointer to the associated DHCPv6 message; callers should check for null if construction conditions are not guaranteed.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4o6::pack
functions.description: Prepares the on-wire format of the DHCPv4-over-DHCPv6 packet. Invokes pack() on both the DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 parts and inserts the DHCPv4-message option into the DHCPv6 message. Use before sending an outgoing DHCPv4o6 message.
requirements: The encapsulated DHCPv6 message (getPkt6()) must be available.
The DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 parts should be in a consistent state for packing (e.g., required fields/options set) before calling.
Caller should expect that the DHCPv4-message option will be inserted into the DHCPv6 message during packing.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4o6::isDhcp4o6
functions.description: Indicates that this packet is a DHCPv4-over-DHCPv6 (DHCPv4o6) message rather than a native DHCPv4 packet. Always returns true for this class.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt4o6::setCopyRetrievedOptions
functions.description: Overrides Pkt::setCopyRetrievedOptions to set whether retrieved options are copied or referenced for this Pkt4o6 and propagates the same setting to the encapsulated Pkt6 instance obtained via getPkt6(). Use to control option retrieval semantics consistently across both layers.
requirements: If an encapsulated Pkt6 exists, it will inherit the same copy/retrieve setting; callers should be aware this affects both DHCPv4 and DHCPv6 option retrieval behavior.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::Pkt6
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::Pkt6(uint8_t msg_type, uint32_t transid, DHCPv6Proto proto = UDP)
functions.description: Constructs a DHCPv6 packet object for transmission (e.g., a server reply). Caller specifies message type, transaction id, and optionally the transport protocol (UDP by default). The object can then be populated with options and packed to on‑wire format via pack().
requirements: msg_type must be a valid DHCPv6 message type number (per DHCPv6 specifications) or behavior is undefined.
If proto is TCP, pack() will throw NotImplemented (IPv6 over TCP not yet supported).
Call pack() before attempting to send; options must be added to options_ prior to packing.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::pack
functions.description: Serializes the packet and its options into on‑wire format, storing the bytes in data_ and length in data_len_. Clears the output buffer before writing. Dispatches to UDP or TCP packers.
requirements: proto_ must indicate a supported protocol: UDP is supported; TCP will throw NotImplemented (IPv6 over TCP not yet supported).
Options to be sent must be present in options_ before calling pack().
May throw BadValue if the packet protocol is invalid and InvalidOperation if packing fails.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::unpack
functions.description: Parses the on‑wire packet bytes in data_ (length in data_len_) into header fields and options, dispatching to UDP or TCP unpack routines.
requirements: data_ must contain the received packet and data_len_ must be set to its size prior to calling.
Behavior/throws for TCP are marked tbd; TCP parsing is noted as not implemented in related comments.
After construction from a buffer, call unpack() before querying options or fields.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getProto
functions.description: Returns the transport protocol (UDP or TCP) currently set for this packet.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::setProto
functions.description: Sets the transport protocol (UDP or TCP) for this packet instance.
requirements: Setting proto to TCP will make pack() (and likely unpack()) fail/not be implemented as IPv6 over TCP is not yet supported.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::makeLabel
functions.signature: static std::string isc::dhcp::Pkt6::makeLabel(const DuidPtr duid, const uint32_t transid, const HWAddrPtr& hwaddr)
functions.description: Builds a concise textual label for identifying a packet in logs, incorporating the client DUID (if provided), the transaction id, and optionally the hardware address.
requirements: duid may be NULL.
hwaddr may be NULL.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getLabel
functions.description: Returns a textual label for this packet instance, wrapping the static makeLabel(). Currently the returned text does not include the hardware address.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::toText
functions.signature: virtual std::string isc::dhcp::Pkt6::toText(bool verbose = false) const
functions.description: Returns a human‑readable string representation of the packet, mainly for debugging. The verbose flag is present but noted as not currently used for v6.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::len
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold this packet (DHCPv6 header plus all options in options_). For received packets, it does not return a proper length until unpack() has completed.
requirements: For received/on‑wire packets, call unpack() before relying on len() (per note in comments).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getType
functions.description: Returns the DHCPv6 message type (e.g., 1 = SOLICIT) for this packet.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::setType
functions.description: Sets the DHCPv6 message type for this packet.
requirements: type should be a valid DHCPv6 message type number (per DHCPv6 specifications).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getClientId
functions.description: Retrieves the client identifier (DUID) from the Client Identifier option in the packet. Exception safe; returns NULL if the option is absent.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getRelayOption
functions.description: Returns an option inserted by a specific relay encapsulation level. Level 0 is the outermost (closest to server); the highest index is the innermost (closest to client).
requirements: nesting_level must be in the range [0, relay_info_.size() - 1]; otherwise throws isc::OutOfRange.
option_code is the numeric DHCPv6 option code to retrieve.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getRelayOptions
functions.description: Returns all options with the given code from a specific relay encapsulation level. Level 0 is the outermost; the highest index is the innermost.
requirements: nesting_level must be in the range [0, relay_info_.size() - 1]; otherwise throws isc::OutOfRange.
option_code is the numeric DHCPv6 option code to match.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getAnyRelayOption
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::OptionPtr isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getAnyRelayOption(const uint16_t option_code, const RelaySearchOrder& order)
functions.description: Searches across relay encapsulation levels and returns the first instance of the specified option code according to the given search order (e.g., closest to client or server).
requirements: order must be a valid RelaySearchOrder (RELAY_SEARCH_FROM_CLIENT, RELAY_SEARCH_FROM_SERVER, RELAY_GET_FIRST, RELAY_GET_LAST).
option_code is the numeric DHCPv6 option code to search for.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getAllRelayOptions
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::OptionCollection isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getAllRelayOptions(const uint16_t option_code, const RelaySearchOrder& order)
functions.description: Searches across relay encapsulation levels and returns matching instances of the specified option code, ordered per the given search order (e.g., first closest to client, first closest to server).
requirements: order must be a valid RelaySearchOrder value.
option_code is the numeric DHCPv6 option code to collect.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getRelay6LinkAddress
functions.description: Returns the link-address field from the specified relay encapsulation level. Level 0 is the outermost (closest to server); the highest index is the innermost (closest to client).
requirements: relay_level must be in the range [0, relay_info_.size() - 1]; otherwise throws isc::OutOfRange.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getRelay6PeerAddress
functions.description: Returns the peer-address field from the specified relay encapsulation level. Level 0 is the outermost (closest to server); the highest index is the innermost (closest to client).
requirements: relay_level must be in the range [0, relay_info_.size() - 1]; otherwise throws isc::OutOfRange.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::addRelayInfo
functions.description: Appends information about a traversed relay (one relay‑forw/relay‑repl encapsulation level) to the packet’s relay_info_ vector.
requirements: relay must contain the necessary relay fields (message type, hop count, addresses, options) as appropriate for a relay level.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getName
functions.signature: static const char* isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getName(const uint8_t type)
functions.description: Returns a constant C‑string with the name of the DHCPv6 message for the given type number. Returns "UNKNOWN" for unknown types. Caller must not free the returned pointer.
requirements: Caller must not release/free the returned pointer.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::getName
functions.description: Returns a constant C‑string with the name of this packet’s DHCPv6 message type. Returns "UNKNOWN" for unknown types. Caller must not free the returned pointer.
requirements: Caller must not release/free the returned pointer.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::Pkt6::copyRelayInfo
functions.description: Copies the relay encapsulation information from a client’s incoming packet into this server response, updating fields as appropriate (e.g., changing RELAY‑FORW to RELAY‑REPL and removing certain parameters).
requirements: question must be a valid (non‑NULL) Pkt6Ptr referring to the client packet from which to copy relay info.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::InvalidPacketFilter::InvalidPacketFilter
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::InvalidPacketFilter::InvalidPacketFilter(const char* file, size_t line, const char* what)
functions.description: Constructs an InvalidPacketFilter exception, identifying the source file, line, and a descriptive message. Typical usage is to throw this when an invalid or unsupported packet filter object is specified or used.
requirements: file: inferred requirement — must be a non-null, null-terminated C-string naming the source file.
line: inferred requirement — should be the source line number associated with the error (size_t, non-negative by type).
what: inferred requirement — must be a non-null, null-terminated C-string describing the error condition.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter::~PktFilter
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the abstract packet filter base class. Ensures proper cleanup via base pointer deletion.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter::isDirectResponseSupported
functions.description: Indicates whether this filter can directly send a DHCP packet to a client that does not yet have an IP address, by injecting the destination hardware address at the link layer (used by DHCPv4 servers).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter::isSocketReceivedTimeSupported
functions.description: Indicates whether packets received through this filter include a SOCKET_RECEIVED event (i.e., support for socket receive timestamping). For direct clients using BPF this is always true; otherwise true when SO_TIMESTAMP is defined.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter::openSocket
functions.signature: virtual isc::dhcp::SocketInfo isc::dhcp::PktFilter::openSocket(isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& addr, const uint16_t port, const bool receive_bcast, const bool send_bcast)
functions.description: Opens the primary socket (for client communication) and optionally a fallback socket (bound to a specific IPv4 address/UDP port) on the given interface. The returned SocketInfo describes both sockets; traffic received on a fallback socket should be dropped.
requirements: iface must reference a valid interface descriptor on which sockets can be opened (inferred from parameter name and context).
addr must be an address on the specified interface to be used to send packets (stated in comments).
port is a UDP port number (range implied by uint16_t). Opening low ports or raw sockets may require elevated privileges (stated in class notes).
receive_bcast indicates the socket should be configured to receive broadcast messages (boolean flag; no additional constraints stated).
send_bcast indicates the socket should be configured to send broadcast messages (boolean flag; no additional constraints stated).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter::receive
functions.signature: virtual isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr isc::dhcp::PktFilter::receive(isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, const isc::dhcp::SocketInfo& socket_info)
functions.description: Receives a DHCPv4 packet from the specified socket associated with the given interface and returns it as a Pkt4Ptr. Implementations may attach metadata such as socket receive time if supported.
requirements: iface must reference the interface associated with the socket used for reception (inferred).
socket_info must describe a valid, open socket previously obtained via openSocket on the same interface (inferred).
Returned value is a DHCPv4 packet; behavior on error (e.g., null return or exception) is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter::send
functions.signature: virtual int isc::dhcp::PktFilter::send(const isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, uint16_t sockfd, const isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr& pkt)
functions.description: Sends the specified DHCPv4 packet using the given socket on the provided interface. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: iface must reference the interface corresponding to the socket descriptor (inferred).
sockfd must be a valid, open socket descriptor obtained via openSocket for this interface (inferred).
pkt must be a non-null pointer to a valid DHCPv4 packet object prepared for transmission (inferred).
If sending directly to a client without an IP address, direct response must be supported by this filter (inferred from isDirectResponseSupported).
Caller should check the return value and handle non-zero (failure) results appropriately (inferred from return contract).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter6::~PktFilter6
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the abstract IPv6 DHCP packet filter interface. Ensures proper cleanup via base-class pointers; subclasses should provide any necessary resource release in their destructors. Typically used and owned through IfaceMgr and smart pointers.
requirements: Must be invoked on a fully constructed isc::dhcp::PktFilter6-derived object (usually via delete through a base pointer or smart pointer).
Subclasses should ensure any OS resources (sockets, joins) they own are released in their destructors.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter6::openSocket
functions.signature: virtual isc::dhcp::SocketInfo isc::dhcp::PktFilter6::openSocket(const isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& addr, const uint16_t port, const bool join_multicast) = 0
functions.description: Opens an IPv6/UDP socket on the given interface and binds it to the specified IPv6 address and UDP port. Optionally joins the All_DHCP_Relay_Agents_and_Servers multicast group when join_multicast is true. Intended to be called by IfaceMgr to prepare sockets for DHCPv6 send/receive on an interface; returns a structure describing the created socket(s).
requirements: iface must refer to a valid system network interface suitable for IPv6 traffic.
addr should be an IPv6 address used to send packets on the iface (typically an address assigned to that interface).
port must be a valid UDP port number (0–65535) appropriate for DHCPv6 operation.
If join_multicast is true, the implementation will attempt to join the All_DHCP_Relay_Agents_and_Servers multicast group.
Caller should use the returned SocketInfo in subsequent receive/send calls of the same PktFilter6 implementation.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter6::receive
functions.description: Receives a single DHCPv6 message using the socket described by socket_info on the specified interface context. Returns a smart pointer to the received DHCPv6 packet.
requirements: socket_info must describe a valid, open IPv6/UDP socket previously obtained from PktFilter6::openSocket of the same implementation.
Caller must handle a null/empty return (if the implementation uses that to indicate failure) or any exceptions according to the specific derived implementation’s contract (not specified here).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter6::send
functions.signature: virtual int isc::dhcp::PktFilter6::send(const isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, uint16_t sockfd, const isc::dhcp::Pkt6Ptr& pkt) = 0
functions.description: Sends a DHCPv6 packet using the provided interface context and socket descriptor. Multiple sockets may be open on a single interface; sockfd selects which socket to use. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: iface must correspond to the interface on which the socket was opened.
sockfd must be a valid socket descriptor obtained/opened by the same PktFilter6 implementation.
pkt must be a valid, non-null DHCPv6 packet object (Pkt6Ptr) ready for transmission.
Caller should check the return value and treat nonzero as a send failure.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilter6::joinMulticast
functions.signature: static bool isc::dhcp::PktFilter6::joinMulticast(int sock, const std::string& ifname, const std::string& mcast)
functions.description: Joins the specified IPv6 multicast group on the given socket, optionally scoped to the provided interface name. The socket must already be bound to in6addr_any prior to calling. Returns true on success.
requirements: sock must refer to a valid IPv6 socket that is already bound to in6addr_any.
ifname should name the target interface when joining link-scoped multicast groups; it must correspond to an existing system interface.
mcast must be a valid IPv6 multicast address string (e.g., "ff02::1:2").
Caller should check the boolean return and handle failure if false is returned.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterBPF::isDirectResponseSupported
functions.description: Returns whether this packet filter supports sending direct responses to clients without configured IP addresses. For the BPF-based filter this always returns true. Typical usage: check capability before attempting to craft/link-layer-addressed replies.
requirements: None beyond calling on a valid PktFilterBPF instance; always returns true.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterBPF::isSocketReceivedTimeSupported
functions.description: Indicates whether retrieving the socket receive timestamp is supported. For the BPF-based filter this always returns true. Use to enable timestamp-dependent processing.
requirements: None beyond calling on a valid PktFilterBPF instance; always returns true.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterBPF::openSocket
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::SocketInfo isc::dhcp::PktFilterBPF::openSocket(isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& addr, const uint16_t port, const bool receive_bcast, const bool send_bcast)
functions.description: Opens and configures a BPF device for the specified interface for DHCP-over-UDP traffic. It attaches the BPF to the interface, installs a filter for DHCP UDP packets, enables immediate mode to avoid read blocking, verifies BPF version, queries kernel buffer size, and (re)allocates the read buffer. Returns a structure describing the primary and fallback socket endpoints to use on this interface.
requirements: iface must refer to the target network interface to attach the BPF device to.
addr is the address on iface to be used for sending; it should be appropriate for the interface (e.g., an address assigned to iface) [inferred from parameter name and comment].
port is the UDP port to bind for DHCP traffic [inferred from parameter name and typical usage].
receive_bcast indicates whether to configure reception of broadcast messages; send_bcast indicates whether to allow sending broadcasts.
Caller should expect the internal socket read buffer to be (re)allocated according to the kernel-reported BPF buffer size (side effect noted in comments).
Must be called before receive/send using the returned SocketInfo. Error/exception behavior not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterBPF::receive
functions.description: Receives a DHCPv4 packet from the specified interface using the provided socket information. Uses BPF to read frames and decode the necessary link/network headers into a DHCP packet object.
requirements: socket_info must describe a socket previously opened for iface via openSocket [inferred from types and typical flow].
iface must correspond to the interface on which socket_info is active [inferred].
On success returns a non-null Pkt4Ptr; specific error/timeout behavior is not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterBPF::send
functions.signature: int isc::dhcp::PktFilterBPF::send(const isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, uint16_t sockfd, const isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr& pkt)
functions.description: Sends a DHCPv4 packet on the given interface using the specified socket descriptor. With BPF, the method crafts the required link/network headers (e.g., for direct client responses) and transmits the frame. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: pkt must be a valid, non-null DHCPv4 packet object [inferred from parameter type/usage].
sockfd must be a valid socket descriptor associated with iface, typically obtained from openSocket [inferred].
iface must be the interface on which the socket was opened [inferred].
Return value 0 indicates success; other return values/errno mappings are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet::isDirectResponseSupported
functions.description: Returns whether this filter supports sending direct responses (i.e., injecting the destination host's hardware address into the packet) over AF_INET/UDP sockets. For this implementation the answer is always false because AF_INET datagram sockets cannot inject the HW address. Typical usage: feature probing before attempting direct responses.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet::isSocketReceivedTimeSupported
functions.description: Indicates whether reception timestamping is supported for this filter. If true, received packets will include a SOCKET_RECEIVED event in their event stack (support is typically dependent on SO_TIMESTAMP being available). Use to gate logic that relies on receive-time metadata.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet::openSocket
functions.signature: virtual isc::dhcp::SocketInfo isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet::openSocket(isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& addr, const uint16_t port, const bool receive_bcast, const bool send_bcast)
functions.description: Opens and configures the primary and fallback AF_INET/UDP sockets on the given interface for DHCPv4 traffic. The address identifies the interface address to bind to, and port is the UDP port. The receive_bcast and send_bcast flags control whether the socket is configured to receive and/or send broadcasts. On success returns a SocketInfo describing the opened sockets; throws on configuration errors.
requirements: iface must refer to a valid network interface object expected by the DHCP stack (initialized and representing an existing system interface).
addr should be an address present on the specified interface (IPv4 address appropriate for AF_INET).
port is a 16-bit UDP port number (0–65535) as provided; privileged or already-used ports may cause exceptions when binding.
If receive_bcast is true, the environment must permit broadcast reception on this interface; otherwise open may fail with an exception.
If send_bcast is true, the environment must permit broadcast transmission; otherwise open may fail with an exception.
Callers must handle isc::dhcp::SocketConfigError exceptions for open/bind/configure failures.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet::receive
functions.signature: virtual isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet::receive(isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, const isc::dhcp::SocketInfo& socket_info)
functions.description: Receives a DHCPv4 packet from the specified socket associated with the given interface, parses it into a Pkt4 object, and returns a shared pointer to it. If socket receive-time is supported, the packet's event stack will include SOCKET_RECEIVED.
requirements: socket_info must describe a valid, open AF_INET/UDP socket associated with iface (typically obtained from openSocket).
The interface referenced by iface must be up and capable of receiving traffic on the provided socket.
Callers must handle isc::dhcp::SocketReadError on receive failures.
Callers must handle exceptions thrown by isc::dhcp::Pkt4 parsing when incoming data is not a valid DHCPv4 message.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet::send
functions.signature: virtual int isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet::send(const isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, uint16_t sockfd, const isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr& pkt)
functions.description: Sends the given DHCPv4 packet through the specified AF_INET/UDP socket. Uses the packet's local address and interface index if set; otherwise relies on routing to select the source address and outbound interface. Returns 0 on success; throws on send errors.
requirements: iface must denote the network interface intended for transmission and be consistent with the provided socket descriptor.
sockfd must be a valid descriptor of a socket opened by this filter (e.g., from openSocket).
pkt must be a non-null pointer to a properly constructed DHCPv4 packet object (isc::dhcp::Pkt4).
Direct hardware-address-based responses are not supported by this filter (no link-layer injection).
Callers must handle isc::dhcp::SocketWriteError on transmission failures.
A nonzero return value indicates failure only via exception; on success the function returns 0.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet6::isSocketReceivedTimeSupported
functions.description: Returns whether obtaining the receive timestamp from the socket is supported by this platform/filter (i.e., SO_TIMESTAMP is available). Use it to decide whether received packets will include a SOCKET_RECEIVED event with a timestamp.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet6::openSocket
functions.signature: virtual isc::dhcp::SocketInfo isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet6::openSocket(const isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& addr, const uint16_t port, const bool join_multicast)
functions.description: Opens an IPv6 UDP datagram socket on the given interface, binding it to the specified address and UDP port. If addr is "::", the socket is bound to in6addr_any. Optionally joins the All_DHCP_Relay_Agents_and_Servers multicast group when join_multicast is true. Returns a SocketInfo describing the primary (and possibly fallback) socket(s). Throws SocketConfigError on open/configuration failures.
requirements: iface must refer to a valid, existing network interface descriptor (initialized).
addr must be a valid IPv6 address on the given interface, or "::" to bind to in6addr_any (unspecified).
port must be a valid UDP port number in the range 0..65535 (type is uint16_t).
join_multicast determines whether the socket joins the All_DHCP_Relay_Agents_and_Servers multicast group; caller should set it appropriately for server/relay operation.
Caller must be prepared to handle isc::dhcp::SocketConfigError exceptions on failure.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet6::receive
functions.description: Receives a single DHCPv6 message from the socket described by socket_info. This call is blocking if no data is available; callers should check readiness (e.g., select) before calling. If the socket is bound to in6addr_any, packets sent to destinations other than multicast or link-local are dropped. Returns a pointer to the received packet. Throws SocketReadError on reception errors.
requirements: Before calling, the caller must ensure the socket has data ready (e.g., via select/poll) to avoid blocking.
socket_info must describe a valid, open IPv6 UDP socket previously obtained for the intended interface (e.g., via openSocket).
Caller must be prepared to handle isc::dhcp::SocketReadError exceptions on read failure.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet6::send
functions.signature: virtual int isc::dhcp::PktFilterInet6::send(const isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, uint16_t sockfd, const isc::dhcp::Pkt6Ptr& pkt)
functions.description: Sends the given DHCPv6 packet through the specified interface and socket descriptor. Multiple sockets may exist per interface (one per IPv6 address). Returns 0 on success; throws SocketWriteError on send failures.
requirements: iface must refer to the interface through which the packet is to be sent (initialized descriptor).
sockfd must be a valid socket descriptor associated with the given interface (previously opened, typically by openSocket).
pkt must be non-null and contain a properly formed DHCPv6 message object.
Caller must be prepared to handle isc::dhcp::SocketWriteError exceptions on send failure.
Caller should check the return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates failure.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterLPF::isDirectResponseSupported
functions.description: Reports whether this packet filter supports sending direct responses to a host without an assigned IPv4 address. For LPF this always returns true. Typical usage: feature probing before choosing a transmission strategy.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterLPF::isSocketReceivedTimeSupported
functions.description: Indicates whether receive timestamping is supported for packets received via this filter (i.e., whether SO_TIMESTAMP is available). When true, received packets will include a SOCKET_RECEIVED event in their event stack. Implementation details are not shown here.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterLPF::openSocket
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::PktFilter::SocketInfo isc::dhcp::PktFilterLPF::openSocket(isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& addr, const uint16_t port, const bool receive_bcast, const bool send_bcast)
functions.description: Opens the primary and fallback raw sockets used to send and receive DHCPv4 messages on a given interface, address, and UDP port, with options to receive and/or send broadcast traffic. Returns a structure describing both sockets.
requirements: iface must reference a valid network interface object corresponding to an existing system interface.
addr should be an IPv4 address assigned to the specified interface (inferred from DHCPv4 context).
port must be a valid UDP port number (0–65535).
If receive_bcast is true, the caller expects the socket to be configured to receive broadcast DHCP packets (inferred from parameter name).
If send_bcast is true, the caller expects the socket to be configured to send broadcast DHCP packets (inferred from parameter name).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterLPF::receive
functions.description: Receives a DHCPv4 packet from the specified socket. Per the header comment, this method currently throws isc::NotImplemented. In normal usage (once implemented), it would read from the socket described by socket_info on the given interface and return the received packet.
requirements: socket_info must describe a valid, open socket associated with iface (inferred from parameter purpose).
Callers must be prepared to handle an isc::NotImplemented exception as documented.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::PktFilterLPF::send
functions.signature: int isc::dhcp::PktFilterLPF::send(const isc::dhcp::Iface& iface, uint16_t sockfd, const isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr& pkt)
functions.description: Sends a DHCPv4 packet over the specified socket on the given interface. Returns 0 on success. Per the header comment, this method currently throws isc::NotImplemented.
requirements: sockfd must be a valid descriptor for a socket suitable for sending DHCPv4 on iface (inferred from parameters).
pkt must be non-null and contain a properly formed DHCPv4 message (inferred from type and context).
Callers must be prepared to handle an isc::NotImplemented exception as documented.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::decodeEthernetHeader
functions.description: Parses an Ethernet frame header from the current read position of the input buffer and assigns the source hardware (MAC) address to the provided DHCPv4 packet object. On success, advances the buffer read pointer past the Ethernet header. Throws InvalidPacketHeader if the header is truncated and BadValue if pkt is null. Intended for decoding raw link-layer frames prior to IP/UDP parsing.
requirements: pkt must be a valid, non-null isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr; otherwise a BadValue exception is thrown.
buf must have at least one complete Ethernet header (14 bytes) available at its current read position; otherwise an InvalidPacketHeader exception is thrown.
Caller must ensure pkt is allocated and ready to receive the client/source hardware address.
Function is intended for Ethernet frames encapsulating IP (Ethertype 0x0800), though non-IP handling is not specified in this declaration.
Caller should be prepared to handle exceptions (InvalidPacketHeader, BadValue).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::decodeIpUdpHeader
functions.description: Parses IPv4 and UDP headers from the current read position of the input buffer and stores the source/destination IPv4 addresses and UDP ports into the DHCPv4 packet object. On success, the buffer read pointer is advanced past these headers. Throws InvalidPacketHeader if headers are truncated and BadValue if pkt is null. Use after link-layer parsing when decoding received DHCPv4 messages.
requirements: pkt must be a valid, non-null isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr; otherwise a BadValue exception is thrown.
buf must contain a complete IPv4 header (minimum 20 bytes) and a complete UDP header (8 bytes) available at the current read position; otherwise an InvalidPacketHeader exception is thrown.
Caller must ensure pkt is allocated and can store IP addresses and UDP ports.
Caller should be prepared to handle exceptions (InvalidPacketHeader, BadValue).
Assumes IPv4; IPv6 is not supported by this function.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::writeEthernetHeader
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::writeEthernetHeader(const isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr& pkt, isc::util::OutputBuffer& out_buf)
functions.description: Serializes an Ethernet frame header into the provided output buffer using source and destination hardware addresses from the DHCPv4 packet object. Intended for constructing link-layer frames when sending DHCPv4 messages. The function does not validate pkt for null.
requirements: pkt must be a valid, non-null isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr.
pkt must contain valid source and destination hardware (MAC) addresses appropriate for the frame being constructed.
out_buf must be a valid, writable isc::util::OutputBuffer with sufficient capacity to append at least 14 bytes.
Caller is responsible for handling any exceptions thrown by underlying buffer operations (not specified here).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::writeIpUdpHeader
functions.signature: void isc::dhcp::writeIpUdpHeader(const isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr& pkt, isc::util::OutputBuffer& out_buf)
functions.description: Builds and writes IPv4 and UDP headers into the output buffer for the given DHCPv4 packet, copying source/destination IP addresses and UDP ports from the pkt object. Intended for preparing on-the-wire IP/UDP encapsulation of a DHCPv4 message. The function does not validate pkt for null.
requirements: pkt must be a valid, non-null isc::dhcp::Pkt4Ptr.
pkt must have source and destination IPv4 addresses and UDP ports set to valid values before calling.
out_buf must be a valid, writable isc::util::OutputBuffer with sufficient capacity to append IPv4 (minimum 20 bytes) and UDP (8 bytes) headers.
Caller must handle any checksum responsibilities not performed by this function if applicable (not explicitly specified here).

functions.name: isc::dhcp::calcChecksum
functions.signature: uint16_t isc::dhcp::calcChecksum(const uint8_t* buf, const uint32_t buf_size, uint32_t sum = 0)
functions.description: Computes the 16-bit additive checksum over the provided buffer (summing 16-bit words), optionally continuing from an initial partial sum. Intended for IP/UDP checksum calculations; the caller must apply the final one's complement outside this function to produce the protocol checksum value.
requirements: If buf_size > 0, buf must be a valid, readable pointer to at least buf_size bytes.
buf_size specifies the number of bytes to include in the sum; caller must ensure it reflects the actual accessible memory range.
sum is an optional initial accumulator value that can be used to chain checksum calculations across multiple buffers.
Caller must perform the final one's complement of the returned sum to obtain an IP/UDP header checksum value.

functions.name: isc::dhcp::SocketInfo::SocketInfo
functions.signature: isc::dhcp::SocketInfo::SocketInfo(const isc::asiolink::IOAddress& addr, const uint16_t port, const int sockfd, const int fallbackfd = -1)
functions.description: Constructs a SocketInfo object describing a DHCP socket binding. Initializes the bound address and port, infers the address family from addr, and stores the primary socket descriptor (sockfd) and an optional fallback socket descriptor (fallbackfd). The fallback descriptor should be negative (default -1) when no fallback socket is open; if provided as non-negative, it represents a socket associated with the primary socket (used typically when the primary is a raw socket). Typical usage: create an instance to pass around socket metadata used by DHCP components.
requirements: addr must be a valid isc::asiolink::IOAddress; its family determines the stored family_.
port is a 16-bit unsigned value representing the bound port.
sockfd is a socket descriptor for the primary socket (int).
fallbackfd should be negative (e.g., -1) if the fallback socket is closed/not open; if non-negative, it should refer to a valid fallback socket associated with the primary socket.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target stubs mostly consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR (arbitrary string) and some numeric FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int/uint32_t).
# Our generator returns a bytes buffer that the harness will slice into strings/ints.
# Strategy: build a compact corpus-like buffer consisting of multiple newline-separated
# tokens that are useful across the targets:
# - interface-like names
# - domain names (partial and FQDN)
# - option-space names
# - hex-like strings
# - small/large blobs for opaque tuples
# - wire-like random bytes blocks
# - textual DNR convenient notation
# Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
SAFE_SPACE_CHARS = ALNUM + "_-"
DOMAIN_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-."
HEX = "0123456789abcdef"


def _rand_alnum(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_iface_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Interface-like: letters/digits/underscore/dash, <=32
    base = _rand_alnum(rng, 2, 8)
    tail = rng.choice(["", str(rng.randint(0, 999)), "-eth", "_vlan" + str(rng.randint(1, 4094))])
    name = (base + tail)[:32]
    # sanitize
    return "".join(c for c in name if c in SAFE_SPACE_CHARS) or "if0"


def _rand_domain(rng: random.Random, full: bool) -> str:
    # Build up to 3 labels, label<=63, total<=253
    labels: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        ln = rng.randint(1, 12)
        lbl = "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-") for _ in range(ln))
        # avoid leading/trailing hyphen per RFC
        if lbl[0] == '-':
            lbl = 'a' + lbl[1:]
        if lbl[-1] == '-':
            lbl = lbl[:-1] + 'a'
        labels.append(lbl)
    dom = ".".join(labels)
    if full and not dom.endswith('.'):
        dom += "."
    return dom


def _rand_option_space(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # valid name per OptionSpace::validateName
    core = _rand_alnum(rng, 3, 10)
    sep = rng.choice(["-", "_", ""])
    tail = _rand_alnum(rng, 0, 6)
    return (core + sep + tail)[:64]


def _rand_hex_from_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return "".join(f"{b:02x}" for b in data)


def _rand_tuple_payload(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    return rng.randbytes(n) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_ipv6_bytes(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 16 bytes
    return (_rand_tuple_payload(rng, 16) + b"\x00" * 16)[:16]


def _rand_dnr_convenient(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Minimal valid DNR convenient config string
    adn = _rand_domain(rng, full=False)
    sp = str(rng.randint(0, 65535))
    addr = rng.choice(["2001:db8::1", "::1", "fe80::1", ""])  # optional
    parts = [f"adn={adn}", f"sp={sp}"]
    if addr:
        parts.append(f"addr={addr}")
    return ";".join(parts) + ";"


def _rand_reasonable_string(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, alphabet: str) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _u32(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    v = rng.getrandbits(32)
    return v.to_bytes(4, 'little')


def _emit_line(lines: List[bytes], s: str):
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR often pulls slices; separate tokens by newlines.
    lines.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    lines: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Several interface names
    for _ in range(5):
        _emit_line(lines, _rand_iface_name(rng))

    # 2) Domain names: partial and full
    for full in (False, True):
        for _ in range(3):
            _emit_line(lines, _rand_domain(rng, full))

    # 3) Option space names: include common dhcp4/dhcp6 and random valid names
    for s in ["dhcp4", "dhcp6", _rand_option_space(rng), _rand_option_space(rng)]:
        _emit_line(lines, s)

    # 4) Short and larger arbitrary blobs for string consumers
    for n in [1, 8, 32, 64, 128, 300, 600]:
        data = (_rand_tuple_payload(rng, n) + b"A" * n)[:n]
        lines.append(data)

    # 5) Hex strings for writeBinary: create even-length hex from random bytes
    for ln in [4, 8, 16, 32]:
        b = _rand_tuple_payload(rng, ln)
        _emit_line(lines, _rand_hex_from_bytes(b))

    # 6) Opaque tuple-friendly small ASCII and binary
    for _ in range(5):
        s = _rand_reasonable_string(rng, 0, 64, string.printable)
        _emit_line(lines, s)

    # 7) DNR convenient notation strings
    for _ in range(3):
        _emit_line(lines, _rand_dnr_convenient(rng))

    # 8) Wire-like packets: ensure min DHCPv4 header length and random v6
    # DHCPv4 min header 236
    v4 = (_rand_tuple_payload(rng, 236) + b"\x00" * 236)[:236]
    lines.append(v4)
    # DHCPv6 arbitrary up to ~300 bytes
    v6 = _rand_tuple_payload(rng, rng.randint(0, 300))
    lines.append(v6)

    # 9) Strings without commas/newlines to satisfy certain sanitizers
    for _ in range(5):
        s = _rand_reasonable_string(rng, 1, 40, string.ascii_letters + string.digits)
        _emit_line(lines, s)

    # 10) Add a few FQDN-like and host-like names for Option4ClientFqdn
    for _ in range(3):
        host = _rand_reasonable_string(rng, 3, 10, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-")
        if host[0] == '-':
            host = 'h' + host[1:]
        if host[-1] == '-':
            host = host[:-1] + 'h'
        dom = _rand_domain(rng, full=False).rstrip('.')
        _emit_line(lines, f"{host}.{dom}")

    # 11) Vendor space names like vendor-<id>
    for _ in range(3):
        _emit_line(lines, f"vendor-{rng.randint(1, 2**31-1)}")

    # 12) SLP scope lists: comma separated tokens
    for _ in range(2):
        scopes = [ _rand_reasonable_string(rng, 3, 8, string.ascii_lowercase) for __ in range(rng.randint(1,4)) ]
        _emit_line(lines, ",".join(scopes))

    # 13) Ensure some non-empty one-char and specific literals
    for s in ["c", "ifA", "example.com", "host", "kea_space", "A", "B"]:
        _emit_line(lines, s)

    # 14) Append some uint32 seeds so that FUZZ_PARAM(uint32_t) reads from buffer get varied values
    # We interleave binary u32 little-endian blocks as separate lines
    for _ in range(32):
        lines.append(_u32(rng))

    # 15) Add IAADDR-like 24-byte body seeds as strings too
    for _ in range(2):
        body = bytearray()
        body += _rand_ipv6_bytes(rng)
        pref = rng.getrandbits(32)
        valid = pref + rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF)
        body += pref.to_bytes(4, 'big')
        body += valid.to_bytes(4, 'big')
        lines.append(bytes(body))

    # Join with newlines to help string tokenization; keep under 4096 bytes
    out = b"\n".join(lines)
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]
    return out

import random
import struct
import string

# Generator for inputs targeting Kea DHCP option/identifier fuzz stubs that mostly
# read arbitrary binary via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and sometimes expect certain minimum sizes.
# Strategy:
# - Produce a composite buffer consisting of several concatenated segments, each
#   crafted to be valid/interesting for different consumers:
#   * Segment A: DUID-like blob (len in [3,130]) starting with valid DUID type.
#   * Segment B: ClientId-like blob (len in [2,255]).
#   * Segment C: MAC address bytes (1..20) for HWAddr/Iface::setMac.
#   * Segment D: Option6Auth minimum payload (11 bytes) with plausible proto/algo/method and RDM.
#   * Segment E: Text snippet (ASCII) suitable for OptionString/Option parsing and convenient-notation DNR.
#   * Segment F: Vendor options short buffer.
# - The stubs will slice FUZZ_PARAM_STR arbitrarily; packing multiple valid slices
#   increases the chance each consumer gets a suitable chunk.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

HEX_CHARS = string.hexdigits.encode()
SAFE_TXT_CHARS = (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._;,:/[]{}()= ").encode()


def _rand_mac(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate a unicast, globally unique MAC-like sequence length 6..20
    length = rng.randint(6, 20)
    mac = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(length))
    if length >= 1:
        mac[0] &= 0xFC  # clear multicast and local bits
    return bytes(mac)


def _rand_ipv6(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.choice(SAFE_TXT_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_hex(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.choice(HEX_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _duid_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # DUID: start with a valid type (1..4), then plausible content
    duid_type = rng.randint(1, 4)
    body = bytearray()
    if duid_type == 1:  # DUID-LLT: type(2), htype(2), time(4), lladdr(>=1)
        htype = 1
        time_val = rng.getrandbits(32)
        ll = _rand_mac(rng)
        body += struct.pack("!HHI", duid_type, htype, time_val) + ll
    elif duid_type == 2:  # DUID-EN: type(2), enterprise(4), id(>=1)
        ent = rng.getrandbits(32)
        ident_len = rng.randint(1, 32)
        ident = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(ident_len))
        body += struct.pack("!HI", duid_type, ent) + ident
    elif duid_type == 3:  # DUID-LL: type(2), htype(2), lladdr(>=1)
        htype = 1
        ll = _rand_mac(rng)
        body += struct.pack("!HH", duid_type, htype) + ll
    else:  # DUID-UUID: type(2), 16-byte UUID
        body += struct.pack("!H", duid_type)
        body += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))
    # Ensure length between 3 and 130
    if len(body) < 3:
        body += bytes(3 - len(body))
    return bytes(body[:130])


def _clientid_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Make option 61-like: type byte + id; but stubs just need 2..255 bytes
    base = bytearray()
    base.append(rng.randint(0, 255))
    idlen = rng.randint(1, 30)
    base += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(idlen))
    return bytes(base)


def _option6auth_min(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # proto, algo, method, rdm(8 bytes). Keep length exactly 11 or a bit more.
    proto = 1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0
    algo = rng.randint(0, 5)
    method = rng.randint(0, 5)
    rdm = rng.getrandbits(64)
    payload = struct.pack("!BBBQ", proto, algo, method, rdm)
    # Occasionally add extra auth info bytes (16 bytes typical hash size)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        extra = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))
        payload += extra
    return payload


def _vendor_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 4-byte vendor id + small blob
    vid = rng.getrandbits(32)
    blob = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 24)))
    return struct.pack("!I", vid) + blob


def _csr_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Classless static route-like bytes: alternating dest/mask and next-hop
    # We will just provide random bytes; consumers tolerate arbitrary buffers.
    n = rng.randint(8, 64)
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _dnr_convenient_text(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a minimal convenient-notation string for DNR (RFC9463)
    # Example: "adn=resolver.example;sp=1;addr=2001:db8::1;alpn=h2;"
    label = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10).decode().strip()
    if not label:
        label = "res"
    adn = f"{label}.example"
    addr = "2001:db8::1"
    alpn = rng.choice(["h2", "http/1.1", "doq", "h3"])
    parts = [
        f"adn={adn}",
        f"sp={rng.randint(0, 10)}",
        f"addr={addr}",
        f"alpn={alpn}",
    ]
    txt = ";".join(parts) + ";"
    return txt.encode()


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    segments = []

    # Segment A: DUID-like
    segments.append(_duid_blob(rng))

    # Segment B: ClientId-like
    segments.append(_clientid_blob(rng))

    # Segment C: MAC address blob
    segments.append(_rand_mac(rng))

    # Segment D: Option6Auth minimum/extended payload
    segments.append(_option6auth_min(rng))

    # Segment E: ASCII text for OptionString/OptionDefinition parsers and DNR convenient mode
    txt = b"vendor-class=" + _rand_ascii(rng, 4, 16) + b"; "
    txt += b"fqdn=host" + _rand_ascii(rng, 2, 6) + b".example; "
    txt += _dnr_convenient_text(rng)
    segments.append(txt)

    # Segment F: Vendor options short buffer
    segments.append(_vendor_block(rng))

    # Segment G: A chunk with multiple of 16 for IPv6 address arrays (for unpackAddresses)
    addr_count = rng.randint(1, 3)
    seg_g = b"".join(_rand_ipv6(rng) for _ in range(addr_count))
    segments.append(seg_g)

    # Segment H: Classless static route-ish blob
    segments.append(_csr_block(rng))

    # Segment I: Some hex text for IdentifierType::fromText users (though stubs use binary)
    segments.append(_rand_hex(rng, 8, 64))

    # Join with small separators that are harmless to binary consumers but help text parsers
    sep = b"\x00\n"
    out = sep.join(segments)

    # Cap to 4096 bytes
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]

    return out

import random
import string

# We need to generate a buffer that the fuzz stubs will read via FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
# The stubs construct colon-separated hex strings from the bytes of FUZZ_PARAM_STR. Therefore, to exercise
# DUID::fromText, ClientId::fromText, and HWAddr::fromText paths with valid data and varied lengths, we should
# return a bytes payload that contains:
# - Several segments of random bytes for use as FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# - Embedded hints to create different sizes (the stubs use rnd.size() to choose length, so our buffer length
#   matters). We'll produce a length between the minimums and maximums used by the stubs (up to 255 and 130),
#   but total buffer can be longer as they only read size() of the string they get.
#
# Since the harness likely consumes the buffer as a whole to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR repeatedly, we'll construct
# a composite bytearray with multiple sections of varied entropy and patterns to cover diverse outputs.

MAX_OUT = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _pattern_bytes(rng: random.Random, patterns, total_len):
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < total_len:
        p = rng.choice(patterns)
        out.extend(p)
    return bytes(out[:total_len])

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose target lengths the stubs will clamp to:
    # DUID min 3, max 130; ClientId min 2, max 255; HWAddr uses MAX_HWADDR_LEN via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    # We create multiple slices of different lengths to encourage different behaviors.
    lens = []
    lens.append(rng.randint(3, 16))      # small DUID
    lens.append(rng.randint(17, 64))     # medium DUID/ClientId
    lens.append(rng.randint(65, 130))    # large DUID upper range
    lens.append(rng.randint(2, 32))      # small ClientId
    lens.append(rng.randint(100, 255))   # large ClientId upper range

    # Build sections with varied content
    sections = []

    for L in lens:
        # Compose each section as mix of:
        # - random bytes
        # - ASCII hex-looking bytes (so colon-hex construction will have varied byte values)
        # - repeating patterns (00, FF, 55, AA) to trigger edge formatting
        part = bytearray()

        # Start with some random bytes
        part.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, max(1, L // 2)))

        # Add hex-looking ascii to vary byte values used for hex conversion later
        hex_chars = bytes(rng.choice(b"0123456789abcdef") for _ in range(max(1, L // 4)))
        part.extend(hex_chars)

        # Add repeating patterns
        patterns = [b"\x00", b"\xff", b"\x55", b"\xaa", b"\x12\x34", b"\xab\xcd"]
        rep = _pattern_bytes(rng, patterns, max(0, L - len(part)))
        part.extend(rep)

        # Trim/pad to exact length L
        part = part[:L]
        if len(part) < L:
            part.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, L - len(part)))

        sections.append(bytes(part))

    # Add a MAC-oriented short segment to encourage 1..20 bytes usage
    mac_len = rng.randint(1, 20)
    mac_seed = _rand_bytes(rng, mac_len)
    sections.append(mac_seed)

    # Concatenate all, and ensure we don't exceed MAX_OUT
    data = b"".join(sections)

    # If still room, add a final high-entropy tail to give the harness extra material
    remaining = max(0, MAX_OUT - len(data))
    if remaining > 0:
        tail_len = min(remaining, rng.randint(16, 256))
        data += _rand_bytes(rng, tail_len)

    return data[:MAX_OUT]

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target: isc::dhcp::DUIDFactory::DUIDFactory
# Fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to obtain an absolute path-like string.
# The interesting part is the file content that DUIDFactory may read as a stored DUID.
# Kea DUID constraints (RFC8415): length between 3 and 130 bytes. First two bytes are DUID type.
# Common DUID formats:
#  - DUID-LLT (1): 2B type(0x00,0x01) | 2B htype | 4B time | link-layer addr (e.g., 6 bytes)
#  - DUID-EN  (2): 2B type(0x00,0x02) | 4B enterprise-id | identifier (>=1 byte)
#  - DUID-LL  (3): 2B type(0x00,0x03) | 2B htype | link-layer addr
#  - DUID-UUID(4): 2B type(0x00,0x04) | 16B UUID
# The factory may read an existing DUID from the storage path; provide valid encodings to exercise code paths.

ETH_HTYPE = 1  # HTYPE_ETHER


def duid_llt(mac: bytes, htype: int = ETH_HTYPE, time_val: int = None) -> bytes:
    if time_val is None:
        # Use a plausible non-zero time value
        time_val = 0x5F3759DF & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return struct.pack("!HHI", 1, htype & 0xFFFF, time_val) + mac


def duid_en(ent: int, ident: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("!HI", 2, ent & 0xFFFFFFFF) + ident


def duid_ll(mac: bytes, htype: int = ETH_HTYPE) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("!HH", 3, htype & 0xFFFF) + mac


def duid_uuid(uuid_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("!H", 4) + uuid_bytes


def rand_mac(rnd: random.Random, length: int = 6) -> bytes:
    # Locally administered unicast MAC (set bit1 of first octet)
    first = rnd.randrange(0, 256)
    first = (first | 0x02) & 0xFE
    rest = bytes(rnd.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(length - 1))
    return bytes([first]) + rest


def rand_uuid(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray(rnd.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(16))
    # Set version 4 and RFC4122 variant
    b[6] = (b[6] & 0x0F) | 0x40
    b[8] = (b[8] & 0x3F) | 0x80
    return bytes(b)


def valid_duid_variants(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    variants: List[bytes] = []

    # DUID-LLT with 6-byte MAC
    variants.append(duid_llt(rand_mac(rnd, 6), ETH_HTYPE))

    # DUID-LLT with 8-byte token-ring style address
    variants.append(duid_llt(rand_mac(rnd, 8), 6))  # HTYPE_IEEE802

    # DUID-EN with ISC enterprise id example (use a common one e.g., 2495 for ISC)
    ent_ids = [2495, 0x0000C0DE, 0xFFFFFFFF]
    for ent in ent_ids:
        ident_len = rnd.randint(4, 12)
        variants.append(duid_en(ent, bytes(rnd.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(ident_len))))

    # DUID-LL with Ethernet MAC
    variants.append(duid_ll(rand_mac(rnd, 6), ETH_HTYPE))

    # DUID-UUID
    variants.append(duid_uuid(rand_uuid(rnd)))

    # Edge sizes within [3,130]: minimal valid (type + 1 byte payload) using EN with 1-byte ident
    variants.append(duid_en(1, b"\x00"))

    # Near-maximum size: EN with long identifier to total 130 bytes
    # 2(type) + 4(ent) + N = 130 => N = 124
    long_ident = bytes(rnd.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(124))
    variants.append(duid_en(0x01020304, long_ident))

    return variants


def wrap_as_file_image(path_bytes: bytes, file_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    # The harness expects a filename pointing to arbitrary data.
    # Our generator returns a single bytes blob. Typical fuzz harnesses
    # split this blob into filename and file content by convention.
    # We create a simple envelope:
    # [4 bytes big-endian path length][path][file content]
    plen = struct.pack("!I", len(path_bytes))
    return plen + path_bytes + file_bytes


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a variant and produce a plausible absolute path string.
    duids = valid_duid_variants(rnd)
    duid_bytes = rnd.choice(duids)

    # Create an absolute UNIX-like path with a stable, seeded name.
    # The harness only needs a string; content is carried in the same buffer per our envelope.
    fname = f"/tmp/kea_duid_{rnd.randrange(1, 10**9):09d}.bin".encode("utf-8")

    # Return envelope containing path and the DUID content.
    payload = wrap_as_file_image(fname, duid_bytes)

    # Ensure size limit
    return payload[:4096]
